News.title: Jailed Albanian mayor uses AI video of himself to pledge free school meals from behind bars
News.content:
Next

AN ALBANIAN mayor has used a deepfake to make a bizarre AI-video, despite being behind bars.

In an Instagram video, Tirana mayor Erion Veliaj used an AI avatar to make a pledge to his voters, promising free school lunches for children.



The post has sparked confusion, not for its use of AI but because the disgraced Mayor is currently in prison awaiting trial.

The odd footage, which Instagram has labelled as “AI content”, shows a digital likeness of the politician standing in front of Albanian and municipal flags.



The AI-mayor claims he has been “held hostage for 20 months”, while he awaits trial.

He says: “I cannot send this greeting except through artificial intelligence.”



The avatar then goes on to list his achievements in office before repeating his pledge to provide free food in schools.

He adds: “However much they want to keep me away from the city, and from you, Tirana is the honour of my life.



“To repay that honour, I will keep working even from the cell where they have locked me up.”

Veliaj’s words drew instant backlash in Albania, with many likening the strange video to the AI-generated speeches made by other incarcerated politicians,

In July, an AI-generated avatar of Jair Bolsonaro, the former president of Brazil, was used during his son’s presidential campaign.

Pakistan’s former prime minister, Imran Khan, made several AI-generated videos, most notably to falsely claim victory in the country’s 2024 general election.

In February 2025, Veliaj was arrested for taking part in a scheme with his wife that took around €1 million in bribes and city funds.



The pair denied all charges against them, which included corruption, money laundering, and hiding assets.

Last month, Albania’s High Court ruled that Veliaj must remain in police custody during the case.

Shockingly, he remains the city’s mayor, despite Tirana’s council voting to remove him from office in 2025.

Albania is also no stranger to AI in politics.

Prime Minister Edi Rama introduced Diella in 2025, the world’s first AI-virtual minister.



The government appointed Diella to the cabinet, tasking her with finding corruption in government projects.

A few months after the announcement, Albanian actress Anila Bisha claimed that her face, voice, and likeness were used to create Diella without her full consent.

She stated that she only agreed to a one-off government chatbot, not a permanent political cabinet role.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Bisha also said she faced harassment and abuse from public backlash to Diella.

The Albanian government dismissed her claims as “nonsense”.

News.title: Family launch fresh appeal after mum, 56, goes missing for two years – ‘darkness clouds every moment’
News.content:
'HELP US' Family launch fresh appeal after mum, 56, goes missing for two years – ‘darkness clouds every moment’







Next

A HEARTBROKEN family have launched a fresh appeal for information after a 56-year-old mum vanished two years ago.

Nazire Koreli was last seen near her home in Welling, south-east London, in September 2024 but her disappearance was only reported to police last year.



Cops have searched her home, combed hundreds of hours of CCTV and carried out underwater searches in nearby Danson Park but despite their efforts, Nazire has not been found.

A man in his 50s was arrested by detectives from the Met’s Specialist Crime Command on March 10 last year.



He was later released on bail and enquiries remain ongoing into the case of the missing mum.

Officers continue to support Nazire’s family, who remain desperate for answers as they mark two years since she was last seen.



A reward of up to £20,000 has now been offered by the independent charity Crimestoppers for information that could help police with the ongoing investigation.

Nazire’s worried daughter said: “To know my mum is to know that she is creative, loves going to concerts, cooking for her family, teaching her students, and above all, loves me and my younger sister, her ‘girls’.

“Mum raised me to be strong, determined and driven. That strength is how I have been able to deal with this heartbreak; determination is what is pushing me to find the answers we as a family so desperately need, the drive keeps me moving forward.

“Since my mum went missing, I have become a mother myself and I don’t know if I will ever accept that they may never meet. My daughter is about to turn two. Two years of a relationship my mother has missed out on, two years of not knowing the most brilliant little girl.



“I am missing not having my own mum while I have become a mum. I want to be able to pick up the phone and call her when I am having a hard day or need her advice. I’m missing our shared history. I’m missing someone to share the emotional toll with. I’m missing our inside jokes.”

She continued: “Since she has been missing, I feel like half of me is living while the other half is frozen in time. There is darkness clouding every happy moment.

“A relentless reminder that a piece of me is gone. I broke into different pieces two years ago, giving my daughter the biggest parts of me, and losing the other parts to the grief and anguish of not having my mother here.”



“There are so many unknowns, and these unknowns make it even more difficult every day. I need to know where my mum is. I need answers.”

The £20k reward for information has been offered up by Crimestoppers in order to help the investigation.

The charity is completely independent of the police and guarantees that anyone who contacts them with information will remain completely anonymous.

The reward is available for three months and anyone with potential knowledge relating to Nazire’s disappearance is urged to call 0800 555 111 or visit the website.

Anyone with information can also contact the police by calling 101 and quoting CAD 5678 of 28 February.



Detective Chief Inspector Wayne Jolley, who is leading the investigation, said: “Two years on from Nazire’s disappearance, her family continue to face the pain of not knowing what happened to her.

“Our investigation remains active, and we are committed to pursuing every line of enquiry available to us.

“Nazire had many friends and acquaintances in the Bexley area. We are asking anyone who knew her, or who may have seen her between September 2024 and February 2025, to think back and contact police if they have any information, no matter how small it may seem.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Nazire is described as a woman of slim build, with light brown hair and olive skin.

“If you have seen her or have any information about her whereabouts, please get in touch.”

News.title: Russia claims it has ‘plague’ under control, Trump says as Don thinks it’s not a bioweapon & doesn’t rule out lab ‘leak’
News.content:
Next

RUSSIA has claimed it has a suspected case of pneumonic plague that killed a lab worker in Siberia “under control”, Donald Trump said.

Scientist Darya Shipilova, 28, died on Friday after being struck down with pneumonia of an unknown cause – she reportedly caught the deadly disease from a broken test tube.



The US president said he would “find out” from Putin about the death after he was asked if it was the result of “a bioweapon”.

Trump told reporters in the Oval Office on Wednesday: “We don’t think so.”



“We’re gonna find out soon enough, but we don’t think so, and if you listen to them, it’s under control.”

After reporters compared the lack of information coming out of Putin’s dictatorship about the disease to China’s initial Covid response, Trump said: “Well China didn’t say much, and Russia‘s not saying much either, but they do say they have it very much under control.”

The US president did not rule out the chance of a disease leaking from the remote Siberian lab.

He said he was planning to call Putin that evening, on the ageing tyrant’s 74th birthday.

The White House is on high alert after the scientist’s death from suspected bubonic plague sparked fears of a global outbreak.

Hundreds are in quarantine, hospitals have been shut down and public events have been cancelled amid growing concerns that Vladimir Putin is covering up the case.



Hundreds are in quarantine, hospitals have been shut down and public events were cancelled in the Eastern European country.

The World Health Organisation (WHO) announced last night it was probing reports of a second case.

WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said the global health body has sought answers from Russia following “reports of a second employee with pneumonia of undetermined cause”.



It comes after unverified reports from Russian media claimed a second person had died of the plague in Russia’s Irkutsk region.

The US embassy in Russia warned Americans about the threat of plague and urged them to leave the territory “immediately”.

It comes amid reports that the US government is growing increasingly frustrated by Moscow’s failure to disclose more details on the researcher’s death.

On Tuesday, Secretary of State Marco Rubio warned the information from Russia was “still quite limited”.

“Maybe there’s nothing there. Maybe it’s bigger than we thought. We don’t know”, he added.



What is the bubonic plague? BUBNOIC plague is a serious disease caused by bacteria (Yersinia pestis) that lives inside fleas riding on wild rodents like rats. Once bitten, the bacteria travel into your lymph nodes – small glands in your neck, armpits, and groin that normally fight off illness. Key symptoms of bubonic plague are swelling in those glands, which turn into massive, painful, egg-sized lumps called “buboes” (which is how the disease gets its name). Unlike pneumonic plague (which settles in the lungs and spreads through cough sprays in the air), bubonic plague stays mainly in the lymph system and cannot usually jump directly from person to person through coughing. Back in the Middle Ages – when it was known as the Black Death – it killed millions because doctors had no cure, but today simple modern antibiotics clear it up quickly if caught early.

A State Department spokesperson confirmed it has “officially requested additional information from the Russian government”.

Fears of a plague outbreak ignited last week when scientist Shipilova died after being exposed to what some outlets reported to be the plague.

She reportedly told medical staff she had accidentally broken a test tube holding live bacteria at Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute.

The scientist then became ill while on an expedition with colleagues in Buryatia, near Russia‘s eastern border with Mongolia.



But Russian health authorities initially failed to confirm Daria’s death, sparking fears of a cover-up.

Russian officials said they have found no evidence her illness was caused by any of the pathogens she worked with, but media reports suggest she may have died of pneumonic plague.

They also claimed a probe found no accidents involving dangerous pathogens and a broken test-tube at the high-security laboratory.

The country’s consumer welfare service said the “sanitary-epidemiological situation” in the Irkutsk region and the cities of Irkutsk and Shelekhov was “stable”.

The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) declared Tuesday it is seeking further information on the Russian case.



But the risk to the wider UK population is considered to be “very low”, UKHSA added.

Putin’s chief infectious diseases doctor Anna Popova rushed 2,600 miles from Moscow to Irkutsk in Siberia to take personal charge of the emergency – but has remained silent.

Health chiefs broke their silence on Tuesday and claimed the scientist had a mystery strain of pneumonia.

She had been diagnosed with a “pneumonia of unknown origin” before her death, medical authorities claimed.

Russian officials say those who came into contact with the researcher all tested negative for pneumonic plague.



Reports say 189 people are in isolation – 114 are in one hospital, 63 in another, and another 12 are at the Anti-Plague Research Institute.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

At least five nearby hospitals are reportedly shut and public events have been axed.

Relatives have been barred from wards with claims medical staff are privately “talking about plague” even though it has not officially been diagnosed.

News.title: Reform did not break political donation rules when party figures discussed foreign cash payments, claims internal probe
News.content:
Next

REFORM did not break political donation rules when senior party figures discussed how a potential foreign cash payment could be handled, according to its own internal investigation.

A report found an alleged £500,000 donation discussed in a bombshell documentary “did not take place” and claimed Reform had not commissioned polls paid for by undercover reporters.



The probe came after a Channel 4 programme appeared to show undercover reporters, posing as wealthy donors, talking to senior Reform figures about disguising foreign donations.

Afterwards, Reform suspended Dan Jukes — an aide to party leader Nigel Farage — and head of policy James Orr.



But now Reform’s probe found “no evidence any laws were broken” by Mr Orr or Mr Jukes.

It claimed Mr Jukes had commissioned expensive opinion polling by himself and admitted Mr Orr was “wrong” to suggest nobody would find out about unauthorised donations.

A Reform UK spokesperson said: “The investigation examined all relevant evidence, including witness interviews, documentary records and electronic communications.

“Having concluded the review, the investigation found no evidence that any laws were broken.”

A Channel 4 spokesperson said: “Channel 4 News stands by its journalism.

“The investigation underwent extensive editorial and external legal scrutiny prior to broadcast. Given the ongoing police investigation, we will not be commenting further.”



A spokesperson for Verbatim said: “We note that this report is an internal one authored by Reform’s own barrister and general secretary, and that a police investigation remains ongoing.

“We are confident in our journalism, which speaks for itself.”

News.title: Evil father, 49, is executed in only European country with death penalty after torturing toddler son to death
News.content:
Next

A TWISTED father who beat and tortured his three-year-old skeletal son to death has been executed, it was revealed today.

Alexander Taratuta, 49, and wife Anastasia Taratuta, 40, were both convicted in 2023 for the cruel murder of their son Semyon.



The father was shot by a state executioner in Belarus, the only country in Europe with a death penalty, while the mother was sentenced to 25 years in prison.

She only avoided death as Belarus does not carry out capital punishment on women.



Andrei Paluda, coordinator of the Human Rights Defenders Against the Death Penalty in Belarus, today revealed that the execution was secretly carried out two years ago.

The country does not officially disclose when convicted criminals are put to death.



The supreme court upheld the death sentence in January 2024, and there was no pardon from dictator Alexander Lukashenko, a close ally of Vladimir Putin.

A court was told how the “wealthy” Taratuta couple inflicted a life of “pure hell” on Semyon, who weighed only 15 lbs when he tragically died.



The helpless child weighed just 15lbs and was described by a paramedic as being “like a skeleton, covered in skin”.

He was forced to sleep on bare linoleum and was often left numb by the cold conditions.

His Russian-born mother regularly punched him, threw him at her husband or against a wall, and hurled objects at him as punishment for soiling the floor.

Semyon was often deprived of food and at times, his hands were tethered as his parents taunted him with food.



A photograph on his gravestone shows the boy with an injured nose due to the cruel abuse.

One court report said: “His parents, instead of watching over him, simply insulted, humiliated and beat him.”

His father denied being cruel and claimed he was trying to “educate” him.

But in January 2023, he kicked Semyon in the head “to make him sit on the floor”.



The terrified boy fell and “showed no signs of life”.

A paramedic later described the horrific state of the child saying: “The boy was very thin, like a skeleton, covered in skin, looking like an African child with a big belly.

“There was an abrasion on his head and a piece of hair was missing.”

The fatal blow resulted in his eye socket being “torn almost to the temple”.

Belarus’ general prosecutor said the couple were motivated by “personal hostility” towards Semyon and had intended to kill him.



The couple reportedly doted on their elder daughter, treating her like a “princess”, while their youngest child was also showered with attention.

After Semyon died, his mother went to a shop and bought lollipops for her two other children.

In his final statement to the court, Alexander said he regretted that his life had “turned out this way”.

He said: “There were no intentions, no conspiracies. I didn’t want to kill, there were no such thoughts.”

He added that he was sorry the last strike was “too strong”.



Belarus is the only country in Europe that still carries out the death penalty.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Those sentenced to death are blindfolded and forced to kneel before being shot in the back of the head – a method which echoes the executions carried out during Stalin’s Soviet era.

Around 350 people are estimated to have been sentenced to death in Belarus during Lukashenko’s 32 years in power.

News.title: Mother and son among missing passengers after US-bound medical plane disappeared as all six on board are pictured
News.content:
Next

A MOTHER and son have been identified as part of the missing people aboard a Boston-bound medical jet that vanished over the Atlantic.

The US Coast Guard have identified Marilyn Lavonne Bean, 66, and her son, Sergio Wayne Lottimore, as two of the six passengers from an air ambulance that disappeared on October 3.



Also among the missing are four Canadians: Philip Gregory Childerhose, Thomas Henry Farquhar, Sarah Jane Paton and Jolene Beth Weir.

The Bermudian mother had suffered a stroke and was on a medevac flight from Bermuda to Boston when their plane was tragically downed.



Rear Adm. Matthew Lake, commander of the Coast Guard Northeast District extended his sympathies to the familes and friends of those impacted by the “tragic incident”.

Sergio was senior vice president and head of specialty reinsurance at Hamilton Re.

In a statement the company said: “The entire Hamilton team is heartbroken by the loss of a respected leader, colleague and friend.”

The aircraft was operated by Latitude Air Ambulance who are mourning an “unimaginable loss.”



President Peter Byl said: “Our focus now is on supporting their families, supporting our people and assisting the authorities.

“We will honour our colleagues by remembering the care, professionalism, and commitment they brought to their work every day.”

The flight left Bermuda’s L.F. Wade International Airport late on Friday October 2.

Harrowing audio suggesting the pilot saying that the plane was “coming in blind” shortly before contact was lost.

The Transportation Safety Board of Canada stated that the crew reported electrical issues near Boston before the jet rapidly descended and vanished from radar south of Nantucket.



The FAA said it initially lost contact with the Gulfstream G100 in the early hours of Saturday.

According to FlightAware data reviewed by Fox News Digital, the plane dropped from 24,000 to 11,000 feet in just three minutes at around 1.00 am.

The US Coast Guard launched a massive search along with Massachusetts authorities and the New York National Guard’s Air Rescue Wing looking for the plane.

Authorities suspended their rescue efforts just a day later after wreckage had been found off the coast of Massachusetts.

Mary Schiavo, a former Inspector General of the Transportation Department, told the AP she believes the plane may have lost its navigation instruments as the storm moved across its path on the radar.



She said: “Something bad happened with this big drop, and they flew into this big storm.

“It’s a terrible place to have a loss of your instruments and be flying blind.

“It’s very easy to get disoriented and not know if you’re turning, climbing, descending, etc.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

International agreements dictate that Canada lead the investigation since the aircraft was registered there.

The National Transportation Board is participating as the accredited representative for the United States.

News.title: Student, 15, wrote notes about ‘hatred of women’ & had ‘interest in serial killers’ before stabbing girl court hears
News.content:
'INTENTION TO KILL' Student, 15, wrote notes about ‘hatred of women’ & had ‘interest in serial killers’ before stabbing girl court hears







Next

A 15-YEAR-OLD schoolboy who stabbed a girl in the back at school had written a note about his “hatred for women”, a court heard.

The teenager allegedly recorded the “motive” for the attack at Thorpe St Andrew School near Norwich as “misanthropy, misogyny, suicide, bullying”, jurors at King’s Lynn Crown Court were told.



Prosecutor Christopher Paxton KC told jurors they would hear evidence about the boy’s “obsessive and dangerous interest in killers and killing”.

The barrister, opening the prosecution case at King’s Lynn Crown Court on Wednesday, said the boy was 15 at the time of the incident back in March.



The teenager – who is now 16 and, along with his alleged victim, can’t be identified for legal reasons – went to the mixed secondary school for 11-18-year-olds with the knife on March 11 this year, King’s Lynn Crown Court heard.

Mr Paxton said that defendant “went to school not to learn but to kill, taking with him a kitchen knife which he used to stab” a 15-year-old girl “in the back”.

The attack, in a corridor in the morning, was captured by CCTV at the school, the court heard.

Mr Paxton described it as a “knife strike delivered, we say, with an intention to kill”.

The prosecutor said the defendant, now aged 16, was “dressed in black, masked up and tooled up with a kitchen knife, striking down into (the girl’s) back when she was defenceless and vulnerable”.

He said the boy was arrested by police and “remained silent” in interview.



Mr Paxton said that by “sheer good fortune” the girl was discharged from hospital the following day.

He told jurors that during the trial they would hear evidence about notes in which he “speaks of his hatred for women”.

Mr Paxton said a “self-generated video” was found on the defendant’s phone depicting American serial killers Edmund Kemper and Ted Bundy alongside a third male.



He said the 17-second clip was created by the defendant using an app and “we say glorifies two serial killers and has them dancing over a still image of the globe”.

Mr Paxton said there was an image of fictional serial killer Paul Spector, from BBC TV show The Fall, with “me btw” written by it.

He also made reference to a saved video from the TV show Dexter, “about a serial killer”, and to a saved image of the serial killer Steve Wright.

The prosecutor said a “handwritten list of names” was found which “has a heading, rather ominously… called ‘victims’ with a question mark”.

Mr Paxton said that in a note written before the attack the defendant said “I really want to do it, really bad, I hate having to wait, I hate it, but I have to wait”.



“I’ve already got a good idea, tomorrow or Thursday or next week. That’s it. I want at least two, maybe three, I would be very proud of five.”

He said the defendant wrote of a “plan, attack on Thorpe St Andrew”.

It continued: “Motive = misanthropy, misogyny, suicide, bullying. Weapon = knife x2? Death = 2+ hopefully, injuries a lot hopefully.”

In another note, Mr Paxton said, the defendant wrote last year: “The idea of violence or possibly even murder sparks something in me.

“I don’t know what it is or what it means either but I think I like the idea of it.



“The idea and look of it inspires me. Maybe one day I will even take my own action of it.”

He said the boy had also written that he had “seen killers being admired, I want admiration”.

Another note said, according to Mr Paxton: “Hate is all you need. Hate is life. Hate is the strongest emotion humans exist with. Love does nothing.”

The defendant, who cannot be identified for legal reasons, denies attempted murder.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Mr Paxton told jurors the boy “does accept… that he intended to stab (the girl) and he accepts he intended to cause really serious harm”, and “also pleaded guilty to having a knife that he used in the attack”.



The trial continues.

News.title: Christa Pike 'angry and confused' after failed execution, lawyers say
News.content:
A lawyer for convicted murderer Christa Pike says that she woke up in hospital "angry and confused" after she survived a botched execution attempt last week.

Her first words were to ask "Where am I?" and "Who are you?", her lawyer Randy Spivey recalled during a news conference.

Pike, who was sentenced to death after murdering Colleen Slemmer with her then-boyfriend in 1995, survived two lethal injections on 30 September in Tennessee.

Experts and her legal team say her apparent recovery is unprecedented, and that no other US inmate has survived a lethal injection from executioners.

A court on Wednesday ordered the state of Tennessee to preserve all evidence related to the failed execution.

Pike, 50, continues to receive critical medical care and is being restrained at her hands and feet in her hospital bed, her lawyers said at the news conference after a court hearing on Wednesday.

Spivey said that her legal team believed for days that she was brain dead, and expected her to be taken off life support at any moment.

However, in a "shock to everyone", she began to talk on Tuesday, while recalling only limited details about the execution attempt.

Pike, he said, had helped the execution team find a vein in her arm, and she was kind and polite while she was being injected.

Then she woke up in a hospital with a tube down her throat and people she didn't know. Both of her arms, he said, are now "tremendously swollen".

"We don't know the toll all of this will take" on her mental health, Spivey said, noting how she was left "angry and confused" by the ordeal.

He added that she also has a blood clot in one of her arms, pneumonia, and is not able to swallow.

Pike is believed to be the only person to survive an execution attempt by lethal injection.

After it became clear Pike would not die, following two rounds of the drug pentobarbital, she was taken to hospital, where she remained unconscious for days as medical staff cleared her body of the injected chemical.

Earlier on Wednesday, lawyers appeared before a judge for an emergency hearing, where her team requested that all evidence from the botched execution be preserved.

That evidence could lay the groundwork for a future lawsuit against the state.

Luke Ihnen, one of Pike's lawyers, began by describing the "roadblocks" that have made it challenging to communicate with his client.

"Up until yesterday our client was unconscious, and unable to communicate," he told Judge Chancellor I'Ashea Myles. Pike is now "speaking limitedly", he said.

Tennessee Assistant Attorney General Will Ayers called attention to the "unusual procedural position here", prompting agreement from the judge. He argued that an emergency motion was unnecessary because the state is already compelled to preserve evidence.

Still, Judge Myles ordered that "anything that was in the actual room needs to be preserved and maintained," including IV lines and syringes, as well as waste, like packaging, inserts, and labels.

The judge also demanded documentation on Pike's psychological condition prior to, during and after the 30 September execution attempt.

News.title: Badenoch says Tories would scrap inheritance tax on family homes
News.content:
Rival parties hit back and said the proposals for IHT, which is levied on the value of someone's estate when they die, would prioritise support for wealthier people in the country.

Badenoch arrived in Birmingham's Symphony Hall with a message to Conservative Party members that they face a "battle for the soul of the this nation".

She argued her party is "renewed" and "coming back" as she continued efforts to convince voters that it has changed following an historic defeat at the 2024 general election.

In a nod to those who have defected to Nigel Farage's party, Badenoch said: "The Conservatives have had an export boom of drama queens going to Reform.

"This party is now the no drama party, we are the no-nonsense party."

With the party trailing Labour and Reform in the polls, Badenoch acknowledged that people are "looking through the shop window", they "like what they see" but "not enough of them are buying yet, we need to fix that".

Her inspiration for how to revive a long-standing brand was Marks and Spencer (M&S), saying they have "adapted their style for today's market and people are flooding back".

Badenoch added: "Just like M&S, we must learn from our mistakes, win back trust and make people feel good about our party again."

One of the biggest responses in the room from members came as Badenoch made clear she did not want to do an election deal with Reform.

She described many Reform voters as "our people", adding: "We let them down and we want them to come back home."

Following a section of the speech mocking some of Reform's senior figures, Badenoch said: "To those who say 'unite the right', we are not uniting with that.

"People deserve better than that and we are going to give them better than that. Character, conduct, and standards matter."

She also said she did not want to live in a country run by people who "debate whether my mixed-race children are English".

In one of many jibes aimed at Burnham, Badenoch labelled him a "Paddington Bear prime minister" who was "hoping that the problems will just go away".

News.title: Burnham to hold security talks with German chancellor in Berlin
News.content:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham will hold talks on tackling cyber-security threats and sabotage with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz on Thursday.

Downing Street said deeper co-operation in the face of rising hybrid threats from Russia would be high on the agenda during Burnham's first official visit to Germany.

Intelligence services in both countries have warned of rising threats, including last month when Germany accused Russia of launching a drone fitted with explosives at Leipzig/Halle Airport.

The Berlin talks come days after Burnham told the Labour Party's conference he wanted to set out options for a closer relationship with the EU later this year, including the prospect of eventually rejoining the bloc.

A German government spokesman has said any future in-out referendum would be primarily a question for Britain, but that Berlin supports stronger ties between the UK and the EU.

Burnham is set to be greeted with military honours at the German capital's Chancellery ahead of his first face-to-face meeting with the chancellor.

On Thursday, the two leaders will formally ratify the 2025 Kensington Treaty, a partnership committing both countries to tackle hostile activity through deeper cooperation on science, technology, defence, security and growth.

Speaking ahead of the visit, Burnham said the UK and Germany were "joining forces to find, expose and disrupt" threats.

He continued: "Attacks on our infrastructure, our businesses and our democracies are not a distant threat.

"They reach into people's homes and workplaces, and they are designed to make us weaker and more divided."

The talks come during a period in which Merz's own political future has come under intense scrutiny.

Burnham replaced Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer in July after the former leader was forced out by his own MPs just two years after winning a landslide election victory.

Similarly, Merz has faced persistent rumours he could be replaced by his party due to his poor approval ratings and following setbacks in regional elections.

Although the chancellor appears to have overcome an immediate crisis in his leadership, questions remain over his future.

The security talks also come in a week when questions have been raised about Germany's reliability as an intelligence partner, following the bombshell arrest of a former spy chief on suspicion of espionage.

August Hanning has been accused of espionage, treason and obtaining classified information for a foreign power, the German Federal Prosecutor's Office says.

He ran the Federal Intelligence Service (BND) from 1998 to 2005 and has since been working as a private consultant.

News.title: We spent thousands on a Tui river cruise but ended up on coach trips
News.content:
David Mallon and a group of five others were due to travel on 21 September. But they decided the new itinerary presented to them a few days before departure was so different from what they had booked that they didn't want to go.

"What they were planning to give us was not a cruise but a glorified coach trip," says David.

One reason for not wanting to accept the new plan was that a member of the group was meant to be avoiding long periods of sitting down - such as coach journeys - for health reasons.

With no offer of a refund, the group booked a last-minute holiday to Kos instead and decided to try and claim money back on their return.

"We don't blame Tui for the water levels, but it's the way they've handled the consequences of that," David says.

He has now submitted a complaint to Tui and says he will take his quest for a refund to the small claims court if necessary.

The BBC contacted Tui River Cruises about passengers' unhappiness with the extensive itinerary changes and the fact they were not offered any refund.

In a statement, a spokesperson said: "Extreme heat across Europe this summer caused low water levels on the Danube, affecting river cruise operators across the region. We review every sailing individually with our nautical partners.

"Customers on the Tui Isla departures on 14 and 21 September were sent revised itineraries before travelling. Where the ship couldn't sail sections of the river, we arranged coach transfers, hotel stays and adjusted travel arrangements to minimise transfer times so customers could still visit destinations, including Budapest, Vienna and Bratislava.

"We reviewed the revised arrangements carefully and customers continued their holiday on the amended itinerary under our standard booking conditions. While customers were still able to visit the key destinations on their itinerary, we're sorry some did not get the river cruise experience they had anticipated."

News.title: Former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro expected to face more charges this week
News.content:
Federal prosecutors are expected to bring additional charges against former Venezuelan President NicolÃ¡s Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores, the BBC's US media partner CBS has reported.

The new charges accuse them of playing a role in the torture of Americans who were held in Venezuelan prisons, according to CBS.

US forces seized Maduro and Flores from their compound in the Venezuelan capital, Caracas, in a dramatic, night-time raid on 3 January, and brought them to New York to face charges for alleged weapon and drug offences, which they deny.

The BBC has contacted Maduro's lawyer for comment as well as the US Attorney's office in Manhattan âwhich brought the charges.

Additional people may be charged for their role in torturing more than a dozen Americans who were wrongfully detained by the Venezuelan government under Maduro, CBS reports.

Maduro's attorney, Barry Pollack, told CBS that he was not provided notice about any additional charges.

Flores, who is facing drug trafficking and weapons charges, is scheduled to appear in federal court for a bond hearing on Thursday in New York.

The trial for both Maduro and Flores is set to begin in June 2027.

The US has accused Maduro of narco-terrorism conspiracy, cocaine-importation conspiracy, and possession of and conspiracy to possess machine guns and destructive devices.

He and 14 others were first indicted in 2020, during President Trump's first term.

Prosecutors have alleged that Maduro, his wife and son, and their accomplices engaged in a cocaine-trafficking conspiracy and partnered with cartels designated as terrorist groups.

They said the accused "abused their positions of public trust and corrupted once-legitimate institutions to import tons of cocaine into the United States".

Maduro has previously called such charges a tool to further "imperial" plans for getting access to Venezuela's rich oil reserves.

He and his wife's lawyers have asked the court to dismiss the charges because he is the leader of a sovereign country and therefore immune from prosecution. They contend the US taking him by force is illegal. The judge has not ruled on their requests.

News.title: Man charged with 13 attempted murders including British child after Alps attack
News.content:
A man accused of attacking 13 people, including a British three-year-old and three other children, with a knife at a playground in the French Alps will go on trial charged with attempted murder, prosecutors have said.

Abdalmasih Hanoun is also charged with armed resistance after the attack at a park in Le Paquier, southeast France, in June 2023.

In addition to the four children, who were aged between 22 months and three years, two adults were wounded in the attack.

The three-year-old British child was visiting the area with her parents. She suffered a single stab wound, French prosecutors said, but was later confirmed to be in a stable condition.

Hanoun will face trial at Haute-Savoie Assize Court in Annecy within the next year, the French public prosecutor's office said on Wednesday.

The prosecutor's statement said: "The defendant will have to answer charges of attempted murder in respect of 13 victims, violence with a weapon without total work incapacity in respect of two victims, and armed resistance."

It added that the defendant's mental state had been assessed by a panel of experts, who found he had not been "suffering from a psychological or neuropsychological disorder" at the time of the attack.

This means there could be "no grounds justifying the decision not to indict Mr Abdalmasih Hanoun".

The statement also said that the decision to order a trial to proceed could be subject to appeal.

Shortly after the attack on 8 June 2023, officials confirmed that the four young victims were in stable condition, including the British toddler.

One of the children was a Dutch national and the other two were confirmed to be French nationals from the eastern region of Haute-Savoie.

Two adults were also hurt in the attack, but were later said to be out of danger.

News.title: Hedgehog among four chosen animals to feature on new banknotes
News.content:
Banknotes are getting a nature makeover - and the Bank of England has revealed the four creatures that will feature on our money.

The Atlantic puffin, barn owl, buff-tailed bumblebee and European hedgehog will appear on the redesigned notes in years to come - although no decision has been made about which animal will be shown on which banknote.

The owl, bumblebee and hedgehog topped a public vote in their specific categories, and the puffin was included to celebrate marine life, the coastline and bring variety to the notes, the Bank said.

Wildlife is replacing notable figures from history, such as Sir Winston Churchill, on our cash in a decision that angered a number of leading politicians.

News.title: Family tribute to 'kind and loving' GP found dead at home
News.content:
The family of a GP who was found dead at her home say they have been "devastated" by her death.

Police discovered the body of Hannah Cain, known to her patients as Dr Hannah Terry, at her home in Dersingham, Norfolk, on Sunday morning.

"She was kind, generous and loving; a beloved mother, daughter, sister, auntie, daughter-in-law and friend," the 45-year-old's family said in a statement.

Her husband, Mark Cain, 45, of Fern Hill in Dersingham, appeared before magistrates in Norwich earlier, accused of her murder.

He did not enter a plea during the hearing and will return before a judge on Thursday.

"We are devastated by the loss of our beautiful Hannah," the family said.

They added: "We are incredibly proud of the woman she was and of the great care she took of all her patients who knew her as Dr Terry.

"We would ask people to respect our privacy at this difficult time."

News.title: Eckert free to stay as Southampton boss as Spygate ban suspended
News.content:
Tonda Eckert is free to continue as Southampton manager after being given a suspended ban for his role in the Spygate scandal.

A Football Association (FA) independent regulatory commission handed the German a six-week ban from all football, but suspended it until the end of next season.

Eckert has also been given a Â£28,000 fine and reprimand but avoided a lengthy ban that could have cost him his job.

The FA had proposed a three-month ban, but the commission gave credit to Eckert for what they called "considerable mitigation in this matter, most particularly around the genuine contrition".

The FA is yet to confirm whether it will appeal.

In a statement, Southampton welcomed the decision.

"We hope this now brings a conclusion to a regrettable period of our history, and measures have been put in place to ensure that such errors in judgement never happen again at our club," the club said.

"We want to take this opportunity to thank the supporters for their unconditional backing throughout this process."

Saints owner Dragan Solak said the club had "already suffered enough".

"We appreciate the panel's recognition of that," he said.

"We are confident the manager has learned from this matter, and a suspended sentence allows him to continue in his role.

"I firmly believe that Tonda is one of Europe's most exciting young coaches, and with this distraction removed, I am confident he can lead the team to a successful season."

Solak said the FA process had been a "positive experience", but criticised the English Football League (EFL), saying "the way they have treated us is not something we will forget".

Saints were expelled from the Championship play-offs in May after admitting spying on training sessions involving Oxford United, Ipswich Town, and Middlesbrough before the play-off semi-final.

They were also handed a four-point deduction for this season.

An English Football League (EFL) independent disciplinary commission ruled at the time the espionage was authorised by Eckert and was a "contrived and determined plan from the top down".

The 33-year-old apologised in June - claiming he was unaware the practice was banned and that it had no impact on his team's performances - but the FA charged him with misconduct, and a hearing took place at the end of last month.

Eckert has been sanctioned for three breaches of FA Rule E3.1. The six-week ban from all football activity would be triggered if he was found to be involved in any other spying between now and the end of next season.

Eckert was appointed permanent Southampton manager in December 2025 after taking interim charge when they were 21st in the Championship. They finished the season in fourth place.

Saints, who face local rivals Portsmouth this weekend, are 13th in the Championship this season with four wins from their eight matches so far.

The FA did not charge Leeds United's former manager Marcelo Bielsa after the club were found guilty of spying on Derby in 2019, instead issuing a formal warning.

The EFL fined Leeds Â£200,000 - which Bielsa said he paid - and introduced a rule prohibiting any club from observing a rival's training session within 72 hours of a match between them.

The most recent precedent for this case came at the 2024 Olympics women's tournament, when Fifa banned Bev Priestman - Canada's head coach - from all football for a year after opponents New Zealand were spied on.

News.title: 'Stop throwing shade' - the woman trying to stop firms leaving the UK
News.content:
The UK needs to do more back its own companies at a time when a growing number are choosing to list their shares in the US rather than at home, the boss of the London Stock Exchange (LSE) has told the BBC.

Dame Julia Hoggett said the government needed to make it "more attractive" to invest in the UK stock market, otherwise big firms would continue to look overseas for their next stage of growth.

Over the last few years, scores of big firms have left the London market, are considering a move or have been bought by private foreign investors.

The fear is this weakens the UK economy by reducing tax revenues and depressing business valuations.

News.title: Man jailed for killing ex days after early release
News.content:
When he was arrested on suspicion of Nurse's murder, Sabat claimed he had killed before and was planning a "murder spree".

He told officers: "I'm a murderer, I don't want to come back out, I wanna go to jail... I've been let out a week.

"Let me back... I'm happy in there, I've done wrong. I killed before and got away with it.

"I've murdered three people so far. I'm gonna go on a murder spree."

Outlining the facts of the case, prosecutor Catherine Farrelly KC said Sabat and Nurse had been in a relationship and had known each other for many years as the defendant was brought up by her father.

Two days after Sabat was released from prison, Nurse's children visited her and on returning home, told their father her "friend or cousin" had been there.

On 22 October, Nurse told a neighbour Sabat was at her address and would not leave. Another neighbour saw her in the street shouting: "Get out of my house."

Two days later, a neighbour heard a single scream coming from the victim's home, the court heard.

Nurse was last seen on CCTV on 25 October. Her children tried to visit the following day but got no response when they knocked on her door.

Her family raised concerns on 27 October and paramedics entered the flat, where the defendant, armed with a knife, charged at a paramedic, the court heard.

The London Ambulance Service crew and family members withdrew from the property and police were called, Farrelly said.

Soon after, armed officers forced entry to the property and used Tasers as they detained Sabat.

Farrelly said officers found Nurse on a bed with a pillow over her face and with multiple stab wounds to the face. She was pronounced dead at the scene.

A post-mortem examination found she had sustained about eight stab wounds, including to the left side of her face, neck and hands.

News.title: Greens investigate party member behind Zionism motion
News.content:
Speitan, a British-Palestinian artist, proposed the Green Party conference motion defining Zionism as an ideology supporting "an ethnonationalist Jewish state".

The motion - which was approved by party members by 1,022 votes to 813 - also called for a "single democratic Palestinian state in all of historic Palestine".

Under Green Party rules, motions supported by members become official party policy, but will not necessarily be included in the party's manifesto at the next general election.

The motion attracted criticism from opposition parties and some Jewish groups, who labelled it an "attack on the Jewish community".

Four out of five Green Party MPs also opposed the motion.

Adrian Ramsay, a former party leader and Green MP for Waveney Valley, said the motion was an "unhelpful distraction" and "wrong in principle" as "the Green Party has always supported the right to self-determination and that has to apply to all peoples".

Asked if he would consider leaving the party, Ramsay told Matt Chorley on BBC Radio 5 Live he was "not ruling anything in or out at this stage".

"What I'm doing at this stage, and we're only a few days after the motion, is to talk carefully with colleagues to reflect both with Jewish Greens but also with Green MPs and other people in leading roles in the party to look at how best can we get things back on track," he said.

On Tuesday, the Jewish Chronicle reported, external the existence of a 2015 letter from Speitan in which she offered to testify as a defence witness in the trial of Minh Quang Pham.

US prosecutors said Pham had been directed by al-Qaeda leader Anwar al-Awlaki to detonate explosives in Heathrow's arrivals area after spending several months in Yemen being trained by him.

He was jailed for 40 years in the US after pleading guilty to supporting al-Qaeda. He denied planning a suicide attack.

In US court documents from 2015, Speitan was listed as a "close friend" who could provide "critical testimony regarding Pham's mental state".

In a later letter to the US District Judge, Speitan said Pham was one of the "few people I regard with such high respect and esteem".

She said if the judge "truly knew the Minh [Pham] that I and others grew to love and respect", they may have "probably had the whole case dismissed".

She acknowledged he "may have had and developed some behavioural issues" but added: "He turned out to be one of the kindest, honest, most sincere, trustworthy and respectful people I have ever known."

There is no suggestion in the documents Speitan knew of Pham's criminal activities at the time they knew each other.

Following the emergence of the letter on Tuesday afternoon, a Green Party spokesperson said: "Where members have expressed views that do not fit in with the party's values, we have internal processes to investigate."

On Wednesday, the party released an updated statement adding "an investigation is under way".

The spokesperson said: "Lubna Speitan holds no party positions other than being a member."

News.title: Fraudster jailed over multi-million pound PPE scam
News.content:
A fraudster has been jailed for helping to scam medical companies out of millions of pounds through bogus personal protective equipment (PPE) deals during the Covid-19 pandemic.

Craig Morris, 43, and Jogesh Bhandari, 60, bought luxury cars, holidays and a new home after pretending they could supply millions of boxes of nitrile gloves in the US and Germany.

They were convicted of two counts of conspiracy to commit fraud by false representation as well as concealing and transferring criminal property at Leicester Crown Court in July.

On Wednesday, Morris received three years and nine months in prison. Jogesh, of Mitchell Drive, Loughborough, Leicestershire, will be sentenced later.

Jogesh told his counsel he was taking a "very extreme painkiller" after having a pacemaker fitted last week and was not able to travel to Northampton, where the sentencing hearing took place.

His wife, former pharmacist Meenakashi Bhandari, 58, also of Mitchell Drive, did attend the sentencing hearing.

She was found guilty of concealing and transferring criminal property. She was given a two-year prison sentence, suspended for two years, 250 hours of unpaid work and 15 days of rehabilitation activity.

Judge William Harbage KC said there was "no medical evidence" to properly explain Jogesh's absence and said a bench warrant would be issued. He is expected to be sentenced on 16 October.

News.title: Eleven arrested as pro-Palestinian marches held in London
News.content:
Eleven people were arrested as several pro-Palestinian demonstrations were held in London on Wednesday, the Metropolitan Police has said.

Among them were five people arrested on suspicion of inciting racial hatred at a protest outside the office of the Board of Deputies of British Jews in north London.

The force said the other arrests were made at student-led pro-Palestinian protests elsewhere in the capital, which went ahead despite calls for them to be postponed so they did not fall on 7 October. One of those arrested was part of a counter-protest.

Wednesday marked three years since the 7 October attack on Israel by Hamas, in which around 1,200 people were killed and 251 others were taken as hostages by the militant group.

Israel responded to the attack by launching a military offensive in Gaza that has killed more than 74,000 Palestinians, according to the Hamas-run health ministry.

Footage from the demonstration outside the Board of Deputies' Camden office showed a few dozen protesters, several of whom were wearing face coverings.

In a statement following the arrests, the Board of Deputies, the UK's largest Jewish community group, said it "would not be threatened or intimidated" and thanked police for their "swift" response.

Slogans "calling for intifada" were chanted during the protest, according to the Met. The five arrested remain in custody.

The term intifada came into popular use during the Palestinian uprising against Israeli occupation of the West Bank and Gaza Strip in 1987.

Jewish groups have described the term as a call for violence against Jewish people. Pro-Palestinian groups have said it is a call for peaceful resistance to Israel's occupation.

The Board of Deputies held a vigil in Whitehall, central London, later on Wednesday to remember the victims of the 7 October attack.

News.title: Masked 15-year-old stabbed schoolgirl, court told
News.content:
A masked 15-year-old who was captured on CCTV stabbing a schoolgirl had written notes saying he hated women, a court has heard.

Police were called to Thorpe St Andrew School, near Norwich, on 11 March, following reports that a 15-year-old girl had been stabbed in the back.

The defendant, who is now 16 and cannot be named for legal reasons, has denied a charge of attempted murder - but has admitted possessing a kitchen knife without lawful authority and wounding with intent.

The boy brought a knife to school, dressed in black with a face mask and had an "intention to kill", prosecutors told King's Lynn Crown Court.

Police were called to reports of the stabbing at 10:24 GMT, not long after parents had gathered at the gates.

Opening the prosecution case, Chris Paxton KC said the defendant armed himself with a kitchen knife and "went to school not to learn, but to kill".

He was "dressed in black, masked up and tooled up", jurors heard.

News.title: Trump tells Texas crowd that wife Melania calls him ‘sir’
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

President Donald Trump on Wednesday told attendees at a rally in Texas that his wife of 21 years, Melania Trump, addresses him the same way as one of his employees rather than using his name or any other term of endearment.

The president was speaking in support of Texas Attorney General and GOP Senate candidate Ken Paxton when he began an extended rant alleging that Paxton’s opponent, Democratic state representative James Talarico, is a vegan, which Talarico denies.

But he quickly went off on a tangent about the pronunciation of “vegan” and recalled being corrected on it by his wife.

“You know, my wife told me ‘sir, you have to do me a favor — it’s not vay-gan, it’s vee-gan,” he said.

Talarico, the 37-year-old seminarian who is currently leading Paxton in most recent polls of the Texas Senate race, has repeatedly denied subscribing to a vegan or vegetarian diet — a lifestyle choice that would be politically perilous in a cattle-raising state such as Texas.

US President Donald Trump speaks during a campaign rally for Republican US Senate candidate Ken Paxton at Freeman Coliseum in San Antonio, Texas, US, October 7, 2026. ( Reuters )

But Paxton’s campaign — and Trump — have repeatedly claimed the Democrat abstains from animal products.

The president continued repeating the scurrilous claim about Talarico’s diet, telling the partisan crowd that his claims to a carnivorous lifestyle are fabricated.

“Now he says he loves meat, but he's a vegan — see, Melania? I got that right,” he said.

“He's a vegan. He wants to eat a piece of lettuce, a little piece of lettuce, please.”

Trump then suggested that a recent absence from the campaign trail on Talarico’s part is because of gastrointestinal illness brought on by eating meat for political purposes.

“You know where he is? He's sick because he's been forced to eat meat for political reasons, and he's throwing up all over the place. He's sick,” he said.

He continued with the bizarre story, accusing Talarico of having “forced himself to go to barbecues” and “stuff some little ribs down his throat.”

“But he'd eat, and then what would happen? He'd go to the back of the tent, and he'd throw up all over the place because he doesn't want meat,” Trump claimed.

The GOP’s meat-based attack on the Texas Democrat stems from comments he’d made to the Texas Humane Legislation Network in which he said reducing meat consumption was "existential" for combating climate change.

At no point did Talarico claim to abstain from meat himself, but that hasn’t stopped Republicans from alleging without evidence that he does not partake.

For his part, Talarico has said he has "been eating barbecue since before Ken Paxton's first indictment,” a reference to the Republican’s long-running legal troubles.

Trump’s appearance in San Antonio on Wednesday was his fourth trip to the Lone Star State in the last six weeks and comes as Talarico has built a lead over Paxton that, if it holds, could make him the first Democrat to win a statewide election there since Ann Richards won the governorship 36 years ago, in 1990.

A recent Sienna College poll showed Talarico with a 51-45 percent lead over Paxton, while a separate Fox News poll also showed the Democrat leading Paxton by a margin of 51 percent to 49 percent.

The last Democrat to win a Senate race in Texas was Lloyd Bentsen, who won re-election to a fourth term in 1988 even as he lost at the top of the ticket as then-Massachusetts Gov. Michael Dukakis’ running-mate in that year’s presidential race.

Bentsen would resign four years later to become Treasury Secretary in the Clinton administration. His appointed Democratic replacement, Robert Krueger, served in the Senate for three months before losing a special election to Republican Kay Bailey Hutchison.

News.title: Tayari Jones' novel 'Kin' wins the Kirkus Prize for fiction, earning a $50,000 award
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Tayari Jones' “Kin,” a novel tracing the life and times of two Black friends from small-town Louisiana, has won the Kirkus Prize for fiction.

Paula Colloff's “Catch the Devil: A True Story of Murder, Deception, and Injustice on the Gulf Coast" won for nonfiction, and Elizabeth Acevedo's “Anger Is Only a Shadow” was awarded for young readers' literature.

Each of the three authors receives a $50,000 cash prize.

Colson Whitehead's “Cool Machine,” Douglas Stuart's “John of John” and Patrick Radden Keefe's “London Falling” were among the finalists.

The Kirkus awards, presented by the industry publication Kirkus Reviews, were established in 2014. Previous winners include Whitehead, Joy Williams and Ta-Nehisi Coates.

News.title: Electric shock gloves deemed too painful by US Army are being rolled out by ICE
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement is moving forward with plans to equip its officers with electric-shock gloves despite an internal military study showing the devices caused intense pain and fear during testing on Army personnel.

ICE signed a $16.7 million contract in August to purchase 6,000 pairs of the devices, known as the G.L.O.V.E., short for “Generated Low Output Voltage Emitter,” according to government records obtained by American Oversight and reported by the Associated Press.

The Department of Homeland Security previously indicated in a public notice that it planned to spend up to $20 million on the technology to acquire thousands of “conductive distraction and de-escalation devices” by March. The contract reportedly describes the equipment as “a low-impact tool” intended for situations where a person actively resists arrest or poses a clear threat, according to American Oversight, a nonpartisan government watchdog group.

Manufactured by Compliant Technologies LLC, based in Lexington, Kentucky, the equipment functions as standard patrol gear until an officer activates a switch. The device delivers an electrical charge upon direct contact with skin, targeting peripheral nerve endings to cause immediate pain rather than the full-body neuromuscular incapacitation typical of a Taser.

According to an October 2024 U.S. Army study conducted at the military prison at Fort Leavenworth, Kansas, test participants playing the role of combative inmates stopped resisting seconds after receiving shocks. The report noted that test subjects were left with “fatigue, soreness and excessive apprehensiveness to being shocked again.”

open image in gallery ICE is equipping officers with electric-shock gloves despite an internal military study showing they caused intense pain during testing, sparking warnings from critics that the technology could lead to widespread abuse without proper oversight ( Getty )

The 38-page report — conducted by the Naval Surface Warfare Center Indian Head Demonstration and Assessment Team — noted that the trial did not produce statistically relevant data to make predictions on efficacy, nor did it evaluate the device’s broader health or safety effects on humans.

The study concluded that “after experiencing the effects of the GLOVE … participants stated just seeing the GLOVE was enough to make them want to comply.”

Researchers observed that although the device did not significantly alter transport times during inmate escorts, it “increased the efficiency” of forced cell extractions and disturbance responses, and it reduced physical exertion for guards.

“GLOVE provides a boost in confidence to smaller or less trained members,” the Army study reported, adding that “inmate compliance was immediate.”

open image in gallery ICE has agreed to pay nearly $17 million for 6,000 units of the equipment, despite internal records showing the agency failed to answer inquiries from 16 US senators regarding agent training ( AP )

However, tests also showed that wet or oily skin intensified the shock, with one participant reporting discomfort lasting 30 minutes.

ICE leaders had access to the study before finalizing the purchase contract. The agency has defended the acquisition, framing the gloves as de-escalation tools that offer a safer alternative to lethal force when handling civil disturbances or subduing subjects during arrests and deportations.

But civil rights groups and lawmakers have raised concerns over potential misuse as the devices are integrated into federal immigration enforcement.

The procurement comes amid a broader expansion of authority for ICE’s Homeland Security Investigations division. Internal government documents obtained by legal advocacy group Democracy Forward and shared with The Independent reveal that HSI has also been tasked with probing voter registration groups and targeting noncitizen voter allegations ahead of the midterms, using data supplied by right-wing activists and federal voter roll databases.

open image in gallery ICE stated that ‘officers are highly trained in de-escalation tactics,’ in a statement to the Associated Press ( AFP via Getty Images )

Advocates warn that giving expanding enforcement powers to the agency increases the potential for harm. Records obtained earlier this year by American Oversight revealed a nearly 400 percent spike in ICE use-of-force incidents during the first months of the second Trump administration, alongside record-high deaths in custody. According to American Oversight, ICE officers have shot and killed at least five people since last year, including two U.S. citizens.

“The military assessment in ICE’s own files shows that these gloves can cause ‘intense pain’ and force compliance. It does not establish that they are safe,” Chioma Chukwu, executive director of American Oversight, said. “Everyone should be alarmed that ICE is preparing to deploy a tool designed to inflict, at best, intense pain, without showing that it is safe for the people who will be subjected to it.”

Jenn Rolnick Borchetta, deputy project director on policing at the American Civil Liberties Union, said in August that the discreet nature of the device increased the risk of abuse.

“ICE spent the last year showing this country they are too quick to use force. Now they will be able to deploy electric shocks with the slight push of a button that maybe nobody else can see them do,” Borchetta said. “Introducing gloves that can so easily be used to deliver terrible pain in encounters is a recipe for harm to the public.”

open image in gallery The ‘GLOVE’ equipment delivers electrical charges directly to skin nerve endings, with tests showing that wet or oily skin significantly intensifies the pain. Though marketed as a de-escalation tool, the manufacturer’s own guidelines explicitly warn against using the devices on pregnant women, children or elderly people ( Getty )

Sen. Catherine Cortez Masto of Nevada noted that ICE has failed to respond to an August 27 inquiry sent by 16 Democratic senators demanding details on deployment policies and safety protocols.

“Without ICE’s responses to legitimate questions from 16 United States senators, the American public is being left in the dark about how these electric-shock gloves are being deployed and what, if any, training the agents who use them have received,” Cortez Masto said.

Proponents of the technology maintain that the devices reduce injuries during physical confrontations. John Peters, president of the Institute for the Prevention of In-Custody Deaths, said that the stimulus was designed to create a quick distraction.

“It’s immediate and sharp, and it will distract you,” Peters said. “I call it like a bee sting. For smaller officers or weaker officers or older officers, I think it has a great advantage.”

open image in gallery ICE officers have shot and killed at least five people since last year, including two US citizens ( Reuters )

Compliant Technologies guidelines state the gloves require biannual recertification and prohibit use against high-risk populations, including pregnant women, children, the elderly or individuals displaying only verbal defiance.

The manufacturer has also faced legal challenges over the device’s use. A pending lawsuit in Kentucky alleges a 43-year-old man died in a county jail after officers shocked him 40 times using a combination of a Taser and the shock gloves.

White House border czar Tom Homan indicated that operational deployment may take time as ICE finishes training modules and administrative policies.

In a statement to the Associated Press, ICE stated that “officers are highly trained in de-escalation tactics,” though the agency did not directly address the findings of the military study.

The Independent has contacted ICE for further comment.

News.title: Last of the suspects in millionaire Florida developer’s plot to murder his estranged wife plead guilty
News.content:

The final two suspects in a millionaire Florida developer’s plot to murder his estranged wife have pleaded guilty.

Sergio Pino, the former head of Century Homebuilders Group, had hired two groups of people to perform escalating attacks against his wife of 32 years, Tatiana Pino, who filed for divorce in 2022.

Nine men were charged in July 2024 in connection with the campaign to stalk, torment, and attempt to kill Tatiana, according to federal prosecutors.

Clementa Johnson of Tallahassee, who was 47 when indicted, pleaded guilty Monday to murder-for-hire conspiracy, murder for hire, stalking, and possession of a firearm by a convicted felon, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of Florida confirmed to the Miami Herald.

Diori Barnard of Miami, who was also 47 when indicted, pleaded guilty to several charges as well, including murder for hire and conspiracy to commit murder for hire, his attorney, Danise Ponton, told the Herald.

open image in gallery The final two suspects in a plot by millionaire Florida developer Sergio Pino to murder his estranged wife, Tatiana, have pleaded guilty ( Google Earth )

When the indictment was returned, prosecutors said in a press release that Tatiana, who was not named, “was subjected to a protracted stalking and attempted murder campaign involving criminal acts to include multiple arsons, poisonings, an automobile crash, and an instance where contract criminals brandished a firearm in furtherance of a plot to kill the victim.”

Authorities believed Pino launched the campaign of violence against Tatiana because of a dispute over their finances, the Herald reported, citing court records and other reports. The Pinos, with their business assets, were worth more than $165 million, NBC 6 South Florida previously reported, citing court records.

Pino died by suicide in July 2024 at his waterfront home in Coral Gables as FBI agents moved in to arrest him. He was found dead by agents with a self-inflicted gunshot wound.

Prosecutors said Johnson told police after his arrest that he was hired to recruit people to kill Tatiana and was promised $250,000 for him and his team, the Herald reported. Barnard was reportedly one of the people Johnson recruited.

open image in gallery Nine men were charged in July 2024 in connection with the campaign to stalk, torment, and attempt to kill Tatiana during a tumultuous divorce, according to federal prosecutors ( Getty Images/iStock )

Johnson and Barnard were set to stand trial starting Monday. Now that the two have pleaded guilty, along with the seven other men who were charged, the tragic case is one step closer to being closed.

Johnson will be sentenced on December 21, according to the Herald. It’s unclear when Barnard’s sentencing hearing will take place. The maximum sentence for each conspiracy and murder-for-hire charge is life in prison, according to the U.S. attorney’s office.

The Independent has reached out to the U.S. attorney’s office for comment.

Ana Quincoces, a former Real Housewives of Miami star who knew the Pinos for decades, told People in September 2024, “Tatiana was always a beauty and a really good mother.” Pino and his wife reportedly had two children together.

“She’s healing, focusing on helping her daughters deal with the trauma and picking up the pieces,” one friend told People about Tatiana’s life after the murder plot and her husband’s death.

News.title: Badenoch revives one of the Tories’ most popular policies – but is anyone listening?
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Kemi Badenoch is attempting to recapture a moment in recent Tory history which spurred her party on to what at the time seemed to be an unlikely election victory.

Back in 2007 the then-shadow chancellor George Osborne spooked Gordon Brown’s Labour government by announcing the Tories would raise the threshold on inheritance tax.

The move at the Tory conference that year scared Mr Brown so much that he ditched his plan for an early election and actually introduced the policy himself.

The following election in 2010, overseen by Mr Osborne, saw David Cameron’s Conservative Party emerge victorious as the largest party and head into a coalition government with the Lib Dems.

open image in gallery Kemi Badenoch delivers her speech to the Tory conference ( Getty )

Now, in her speech almost 20 years later, Ms Badenoch used the hatred of inheritance tax again to try to fuel what appears to be an unlikely Tory revival, with the party languishing at around 20 per cent in the polls and in third place behind both Labour and Reform UK.

The Tories argue that, contrary to current figures that only one in five people are affected by inheritance tax, that figure is about to rise to 16 per cent due to rising housing costs.

The idea of lifting family homes out of inheritance tax altogether, as well making the first £1m of assets tax free, especially helps spark a potential revival in London and the south east of England where property prices are high but the party has lost out to the Lib Dems, Labour and Reform.

This is very much about cementing Tory support back in its former heartlands.

But it will not help them in places such as East Anglia or the north or England and the Midlands where they are still losing out to Reform.

Those who want Ms Badenoch to reach out more to working class voters will be unhappy that aspiration is limited to the well off, without considering tax cuts which help more people, such as a penny off income tax.

But this is a pledge that is very much about a party that is rebuilding from a low base in a political landscape more fractured than at any other time in modern British history.

open image in gallery George Osborne made an inheritance tax pledge in 2007 which spooked Gordon Brown ( Getty )

The speech though was not just about tax cuts. Ms Badenoch had a lot to get off her chest, dipping into several topic areas including the rise of racism, the need for more prison spaces in Britain’s overcrowded jails and dealing with Nigel Farage and Reform.

There was a very clear message to Tory MPs who have been chuntering this week and before about the need to “unite the right” – the answer is “no!”

Ms Badenoch launched a ferocious attack on Reform and its “dodgy donations”, suggesting that they are now “measuring the curtains” for prison cells not Downing Street.

But her line, “for those people who say unite the right, I say not with them” is aimed at the many MPs and former MPs, especially on the right of the party who have been pushing for a deal with Reform.

Most prominent has been Jacob Rees-Mogg but there have been others who have openly discussed it at conference.

Ms Badenoch’s “we are the Conservative Party” is a message to them all that the Tories will not be shaking hands with Nigel Farage to secure a place in No 10.

Overall though there was an important difference in tone with Andy Burnham who she mocked mercilessly from the stage.

When the prime minister gave his speech at the Labour Party conference in Liverpool last week it was clear he was speaking to the activists in the room more than the audience watching outside.

He even admitted as much in his speech.

open image in gallery Badenoch wants no deal with Reform UK leader Nigel Farage (Dominic Lipinski/PA) ( PA Wire )

But Ms Badenoch is projecting her message to the audience outside promising a political fight and attacking a Labour government coming after you with higher taxes.

The approaches represent the different needs of the two leaders. Mr Burnham needed to heal a wounded party after Keir Starmer’s ousting, while Ms Badenoch needs to persuade a country still sceptical of the Tories that they are worthy of governing again.

But perhaps the biggest conclusion is that this is now Ms Badenoch’s party.

She was comfortable, warm and confident on the stage with the audience responding to her almost as well as chairman Kevin Hollinrake’s labrador Zuzu.

The Tory leader was able to emphasise her desire for real Conservatives to represent the party at the next election.

And her viral moment of telling Wes Streeting “do your job” earlier this year was something she leaned into a lot in this speech.

She listed out her shadow cabinet members who “did their job”, such as shadow justice secretary Nick Timothy forcing a Labour U-turn on jury trials, or shadow environment secretary Victoria Atkins forcing a U-turn on the family farm tax.

She has listed the qualities she wants in candidates standing at the next election, but number one is “people who know how to get stuff done, not just talk a good game”.

Ms Badenoch knows that her party suffers from a sense among the public that they failed to do what they promised to do in government.

She wants a change of culture and a return to one of aspiration.

But with polling showing the Tories falling further behind in the polls, it remains to be seen whether it will it be enough to turn the party’s fortunes around.
