World.title: Presidency admits more Nigerians fell into poverty under Tinubu
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu

By Dickson Omobola

The Presidency, Wednesday, acknowledged that more Nigerians have been pushed into poverty under the administration of President Bola Tinubu, but said the situation is a consequence of the reforms being implemented by government.

The Presidency also faulted a report by The Economist on Nigerians’ dissatisfaction with Tinubu’s performance, describing it as watery and lacking substance.

On October 1, The Economist said President Tinubu might win the forthcoming 2027 polls despite public discontent.

The report, titled: ‘Nigerians dislike their president, but may re-elect him anyway’, identified a worsening security crisis, the biting

effects of the economic reforms and popular political challengers as factors that could work against the president’s re-election bid.

Reacting to the report on Politics Today, a Channels TV programme, Special Adviser to President Tinubu on Policy Communication, Daniel Bwala, questioned the research methodology of the report.

Bwala said: “Let me say that The Economist’s theory, as published, is watery. It doesn’t have the substance. If you want to write an opinion piece, and especially when you want to rely on data, you want to make a claim on the data, the first thing you should do is to conduct a survey. There would be some people who don’t like him (Tinubu), but there are others who like him.

“In other words, in democracy you have to allow the two voices to speak. When you make a claim that Nigerians don’t like him (Tinubu) without also saying that there are a lot of people, for example, one million families whose children have benefited from Nigerian Education Loan Fund, NELFUND, do you think they hate him? If you look at the agricultural sector in Nigeria, the kind of incentive and benefit they got, do you think they hate him? What about the incentive for the manufacturers in production?”

Asked whether more people had been thrown into poverty by the current administration, he said: “Do you know why? It is simply because we took a reform. There is no part of the world where reform comes with convenience. The population is 230 million, already at some stage of poverty. But we can’t make any progress until reform is carried out. None of the presidents that came before this president had the courage to do it because of fear.

“But the president said we can’t make any progress. So, he took that reform. Please let it be clear, even to the opposition. The reason why you have this number of poor people, and some of these doomsday analyses that people are giving, is because we undertook a reform. There is no part of the world where you start a reform like that, and there will not be discomfort. More people went down to poverty. I acknowledge it, I’m not doubting. But, there is a but to it. Since the reform started till today, we have made marked progress, which is what we have spent the last three years doing.”

Vanguard News

World.title: Former Spurs defender Vega to stand for FIFA presidency
World.content:
Former Tottenham defender Ramon Vega has become the first person to announce he intends to run against incumbent Gianni Infantino in the FIFA presidential election next year.

The 55-year-old former Switzerland centre-back has been working in finance since he retired in 2004.

It is not the first time, though, that Vega has announced his intention to run for the top job at world football’s governing body.

He had considered running against Infantino following the resignation of Sepp Blatter in the wake of a corruption scandal in 2015.

And he tried to challenge his fellow Swiss in 2022, but failed to garner sufficient support to make it onto the ballot.

“The situation has evolved a lot since then,” Vega told AFP, adding FIFA’s member associations were “much more open to change” than when he previously sought to stand.

“I am standing because my life has prepared me to serve the game,” Vega added in an 11-page dossier announcing his candidacy.

“I believe I have a duty and a social responsibility to protect and defend football — its integrity, its people and its future.”

Pressure has been building on Infantino, who has lost the support of numerous FIFA member associations, since his aborted plan to create a commercial subsidiary to run FIFA’s biggest events, such as the World Cup and Club World Cup.

Last week, the Swiss Football Association became the latest to withdraw its support for Infantino, citing concerns over his record on transparency, accountability and institutional responsibility.

“Faith and trust across the football family have been deeply damaged,” said Vega in his dossier.

“We must rebuild both, restore FIFA’s credibility and reunite the global football family.”

It is not clear whether Vega would be able to stand.

He must first gain the backing of at least five of FIFA’s 211 member federations, but also be proposed by one of those.

And the rules stipulate a candidate must have been involved in football for two of the previous five years, and pass an eligibility review.

Potential candidates have until November 18 to meet those criteria.

World.title: NYSC: Oyo urges FG to intensify action against kidnappers after release of 20 PCMs
World.content:
Gov Seyi Makinde

By Adeola Badru

The Oyo State Government has welcomed the release of the 20 prospective members of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) who were abducted while travelling to their orientation camps in Imo State, but urged the Federal Government to intensify efforts to tackle the persistent wave of kidnapping and banditry across the country.

The Commissioner for Information and Orientation, Mr. Dotun Oyelade, made the call while reacting to the release of the prospective corps members by their abductors on Wednesday, saying the development had brought relief to the state government, the affected families and the people of Oyo State.

Oyelade said, “Oyo State Government is relieved at the release of our children from the bondage of abduction once again.”

He congratulated the Imo and Oyo State Governments, as well as the Federal Government, over the release, while stressing that the development should also serve as a reminder of the need for stronger and more coordinated action against the growing insecurity in the country.

“We congratulate the Imo and Oyo State Governments and the Federal Government too,” he said.

The commissioner, however, said the Federal Government, which he described as having the greatest constitutional powers and capacity to address the security challenge, needed to do more to prevent such incidents from recurring.

According to him, “The Federal Government, which has the preponderance of power and capacity to effectively nip this embarrassing development in the bud, must be more proactive and live up to its promise to keep citizens safer across the land.”

Oyelade expressed concern that despite repeated assurances from the Presidency on efforts to improve national security, kidnapping and banditry continued to affect communities and citizens in different parts of the country.

“It is worrisome that large pockets of kidnappings and banditry still dominate the Nigerian landscape, the constant robust assurances from the Presidency notwithstanding,” he said.

He further raised concern over the number of Nigerians who, according to him, remained in captivity in forests across the country, saying the continued abduction of citizens underscored the need for more effective security measures.

“At the last count, not less than 200 Nigerians are still languishing in forests, abducted in circumstances in which government appears to have no clue,” the commissioner said.

The 20 prospective corps members were abducted while travelling to Imo State for the NYSC orientation exercise, causing anxiety among their families and loved ones and prompting efforts to secure their release.

Their release was confirmed on Wednesday by the Olubadan of Ibadanland, Oba Rashidi Ladoja, who received the information from Imo State Governor, Mr. Hope Uzodinma, during a telephone conversation at about 5pm.

The development was conveyed to the Olubadan by Governor Uzodinma personally, according to a statement by the monarch’s media aide, Adeola Oloko.

The Olubadan, who had closely monitored developments surrounding the abduction, expressed relief following confirmation that the prospective corps members had regained their freedom.

Vanguard News

World.title: Customer Satisfaction Up 71% as E-commerce, Others Emerge Best Sectors
World.content:
Emma Okonji

As the country celebrates 2026 Customer Service Week, the Nigeria Customer Service Index (NCSI) Group has released its 2025 report on the state of customer service in Nigeria.

According to the report, customer satisfaction score hits all-time high at 71 per cent amid service quality decline in key sectors, as E-commerce, Real Estate and Telecommunications emerged best sectors, among the 12 sectors surveyed by the report.

The 2025 report, which is the third in its series since its debut in 2023, presented a contrasting yet predictable outcomes with resilient performance amid wide service quality decline.

Powered by the West Africa Association of Customer Service Professionals (WAACSP), the report is a national benchmark of customer satisfaction, service delivery and consumer sentiment across 12 major economic sectors.

The report, which was jointly signed by the Head, Media & Communications, NCSI Group, Orode Jennifer, and Team Lead, NCSI Group, Anozie Christian, is a template that offers organisations a practical basis for comparing performance, understanding changing expectations and directing service-improvement investments.

Using a structured, web-based questionnaire, quantitative research and random sampling, the 2025 survey gathered 21,387 responses, rating over 1,500 organisations, covering all 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT).

The report said respondents evaluated their experiences across customer experience dimensions including trust, professionalism, competence, complaint resolution, ease of doing business, processes and procedures, staff engagement, and customer-focused innovation.

Key findings of the report showed that the national NCSI benchmark stood at 71 per cent, with nine of the 12 sectors recording lower scores than the previous reporting period.

E-commerce led the sector performance at 75 per cent, rising 15 percentage points from 2024, followed by Real Estate at 72 per cent, up 10 points, while Telecommunications posted modest positive growth of one point.

The sharpest contractions were recorded in Transportation (-13 points), Power (-10 points) and the Public Sector (-10 points). Public Sector and Power recorded the lowest scores overall, at 53 per cent and 51 per cent, respectively. Customer trust was the number-one priority in every sector, ranging from 71 per cent in Power to 90 per cent in E-commerce. Hospitality recorded the strongest positive public impression at 69 per cent, while negative sentiment was highest in the Public Sector (44 per cent) and Power (43 per cent).

From the performance scorecard, the Military Hospital Kaduna came top in the public healthcare subsector, while Stanbic IBTC came top in the banking subsector, upstaging Wema Bank (1st in 2024) to 3rd, while FCMB joined in at 2nd place.

Slot moved to the top spot in the E-commerce sector, as did BetKing in the sports/entertainment sector.

MTN (GSM), OPay (fintech), Eko Hotels (hospitality), Covenant University (private education), Ibom Air (aviation), Obafemi Awolowo University (OAU) Ile-Ife (public universities) all maintained their top spot from the 2024 report.

Giving the performance scorecard for 2025, NCSI and WAACSP recommended that organisations prioritise trust-building, faster complaint resolution and consistent service delivery especially in the public sector and power. They also called for hybrid customer-service strategies that combine digital convenience with reliable traditional support.

The report advised that organisations could use the index to benchmark performance year over year, identify the service dimensions that most need attention and sequence investments in frontline training, transparent processes and responsive customer channels. For stronger future comparisons, the report also pointed to the value of broader participation outside Lagos and Abuja.

From the participation profile, the report explained that financial services and telecommunications generated the largest response volumes, although every sector saw year-on-year growth in participation, adding that Enugu, Oyo and Rivers states are among the next leading locations.

The report however noted that concentration in Lagos and Abuja, uneven response volumes and unmet quotas in some sectors should be considered when interpreting results and planning future sampling.

World.title: Zoho Nigeria Harps on Data Control amid AI Adoption
World.content:
Country Head, Zoho Nigeria, Mr. Kehinde Ogundare, has advised Nigerian businesses to take a more active approach in understanding and controlling their data amid increase in the adoption of cloud and Artificial Intelligence (AI).

Ogundare gave the advice during a fireside chat with Managing Editor of Techeconomy, Joan Aimuengheuwa, at the debut GrowthX by Techeconomy in Lagos, where they discussed enterprise technology and data privacy.

Ogundare encouraged businesses to look beyond regulatory compliance and consider where their data is stored, who can access it, how it is being used, and the level of control they have over their information.

“From a business owner’s standpoint, what is your understanding of data sovereignty? What do you know about your data? Do you know where it is stored? Do you know how it is being used? Who is processing your data? Who is accessing it and what kind of control you have over it?”, Ogundare asked.

World.title: Firm Launches Commerce Platform to Connect 774 LGAs
World.content:
Chastest Consult Limited has announced the launch of LGA Connect Nigeria, a first-of-its-kind civic and commerce platform that brings all 774 Local Government Areas across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) into a single digital ecosystem for Nigerians at home and in the diaspora.

The platform, which went live this week on web and mobile, allows any Nigerian, from a farmer in Ikot Ekpene to a nurse in Manchester, to find their home LGA, interact in indigenous languages, transact securely, and engage directly with their local council leadership.

According to the company, LGA Connect is designed to solve two long-standing gaps: the low online visibility of local governments, which is the tier of governance that most impacts daily life, and the lack of structured coordination for an estimated 17 million Nigerians abroad who remit tens of billions of dollars home annually without a direct channel to their communities.

Speaking on the launch, Regional Director at Chastest Consult, Ini Archibong, said the platform would address Nigeria’s core challenge of coordination.

“Nigeria does not have a talent problem, an ambition problem or a diaspora problem. It has a coordination problem. For too long, the tools our people used to organise, transact and hold power to account were built for someone else’s country. LGA Connect is built for us, at the level where governance actually touches life,” Archibong said.

World.title: NCC Leverages ITU’s Recognition to Advance Digital Literacy
World.content:
The Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC) has said it will leverage the Digital Bridge Institute’s (DBI) designation as an International Telecommunication Union (ITU) Digital Transformation Centre (DTC) to accelerate digital literacy, enhance digital inclusion, and equip more Nigerians with the skills needed to participate effectively in the digital economy.

NCC made this known while receiving the Senior Digital Skills Officer of the ITU, Ms. Robyn Fysh, who paid a courtesy visit to the NCC Head Office in Abuja, recently.

The visit took place on the sidelines of Fysh’s official engagement in Nigeria. The engagement forms part of her mission to DBI following the Institute’s designation by the ITU as a Digital Transformation Centre (DTC), a recognition that places DBI within a global network of institutions dedicated to advancing digital skills and digital transformation initiatives. DBI also serves as the ITU’s Digital Training Academy (DTA) in Nigeria.

Representing the Executive Vice Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of the NCC, Dr. Aminu Maida, the Director, Research and Development, Babagana Digima, received Fysh and members of the DBI delegation led by its President and Chief Executive Officer, Mr. David Daser.

Digima reaffirmed the commission’s commitment to innovation, capacity development, and digital transformation. He noted that DBI’s designation as an ITU Digital Transformation Centre presented a significant opportunity to deepen collaboration among the NCC, DBI and the ITU in advancing digital skills development and digital inclusion across the country.

“DBI’s recognition as an ITU Digital Transformation Centre is a significant milestone for Nigeria’s digital skills ecosystem and an opportunity to expand access to digital literacy and capacity-building programmes across the country,” he said.

World.title: PMI to Assist Entrepreneurs Turn Ideas into Viable Businesses
World.content:
Project Management Institute (PMI), the leading authority in project success, has launched a free course to help entrepreneurs across sectors build delivery skills such as planning, financial discipline, and reliability.

Titled: ‘PMI Foundations: Project Management for Entrepreneurs’, the course is designed for aspiring and early-stage entrepreneurs across sectors, including founders, side-hustle creators, solopreneurs, community innovators and small teams.

Giving details of the report findings, the Managing Director, sub-Saharan Africa at PMI, George Asamani, said: “These findings show why creators need support with the business behind their content. A brand deal can bring in revenue, but creators also need to understand what it will cost to deliver. Project management helps them plan that work and use their resources wisely. Those skills matter just as much to someone building a catering business or launching a new product.”

The report found that creators faced irregular income, uncertain payment dates, and production costs that impacted their earnings. Against this backdrop, the course’s ‘Before You Begin’ and ‘Know Your Numbers’ modules address practical questions about readiness, resources and financial decisions. For a creator, accepting a campaign may mean paying an editor or hiring equipment before payment arrives. Planning costs and understanding cash flow can help them assess whether they can afford to take on the work and what they will need to deliver it, Asamani said. According to him, as a creator’s business grows, balancing content production with the demands of running it can become exhausting, especially when every task and decision still rests with one person.

World.title: NGSTQB Backs National Software Testing Guideline, Seeks Enforcement
World.content:
The Nigerian Software Testing Qualifications Board (NGSTQB) has formally endorsed the National Software Testing Guideline introduced by the National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA), while urging its enforcement follows a risk-based, tiered model rather than a one-size-fits-all standard.

The guideline requires software developed, modified, integrated or deployed for use in Nigeria to undergo functional and non-functional testing, covering security, performance, usability, compatibility, reliability, maintainability and portability, before operational deployment. It applies across both public and private sectors, with the depth of testing determined by a system’s risk, data sensitivity, public exposure and potential consequences of failure.

NGSTQB, a professional body focused on software testing standards and certification in Nigeria, said the guideline would address a gap in the country’s digital economy, where software failures have disrupted banking, identity and public-service platforms relied on by millions of Nigerians.

President of NGSTQB, Mr. Boye Dare, said: “Software has become the invisible infrastructure of Nigeria’s economy, it sits behind every bank transfer, every hospital record, every government portal. When that infrastructure is not properly tested, the cost is not abstract; it is failed transactions, exposed data and public services that let people down. NGSTQB gives its full support to NITDA’s objective of ensuring that software used in Nigeria is secure, reliable and fit for purpose.”

The board said its support remained anchored on five positions: full backing for the guideline’s objectives and implementation; alignment with NITDA’s aim of ensuring software meets defined standards of quality, security and performance; support for independent, competent and accountable testing of systems whose failure could materially affect citizens or critical infrastructure; a call for proportionate, risk-based regulation so that assurance effort matches potential harm rather than applying uniformly across all software; and a call on industry to treat compliance as a market-enabling investment rather than a late-stage certification exercise.

World.title: Oloworara: Pencom Additional N10.7tn Retirement Wealth  in Two Years
World.content:
Ebere Nwoji

The Director General National Pension Commisssion (PenCcom), Ms Omolola Oloworara, has revealed that the agency created additional N10.7 trillion retirement wealth in the last two years.

Oloworara who stated this at the 2026 annual media conference organised by PenCom in Lagos, said the quantum growth recorded in the industry was enabled by various reforms going on in the pension sector.

According to her, “The reforms also saw significant growth in retirees’ take-home benefits especially retirees under treasury funded pension scheme and those under National Social Insurance Trust scheme in which no less that 2,116 retirees received 1,173 per cent increase in their take home benefits thereby relieving the beneficiaries from 21 years of stagnation in pension benefit.”

She said 938,229 Nigerians joined the Contributory Pension Scheme(CPS) within the same period, adding that this has expanded the pool of formal retirement savings.

She said monthly pension payments for more than 241,000 retirees increased from N12.15 billion to N14.83 billion following the implementation of pension adjustments, an aspect of the reform going on in the sector.

Oloworaran disclosed that, Treasury-funded Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs) now have an exit benefit scheme.

Under the scheme, which took effect from January 1, 2026, eligible employees with at least 10 years of qualifying service receive an additional benefit equivalent to 100 per cent of their total emolument, on top of their normal pension benefits.

She said, the first 175 retirees had already received approximately N1.1 billion under the scheme, adding that this is a full year’s pay as an additional benefit describing it as a demonstration of government’s commitment to workers and retirees.

She said zero tolerance to delayed pension payment which was also an aspect of the pension sector reforms has reduced the time required to process retirement benefits.

According to her, retirement benefits that previously took as long as 21 months to approve are now processed within 48 hours for eligible Federal Government workers.

She added that private-sector retirement benefits, which previously took at least two weeks even under the fastest circumstances, are also now being approved within 48 hours.

World.title: EFCC: Right Policy, Regulation Will Tame Cybercrime Without Enforcement
World.content:
Emma Okonji

The Executive Chairman, Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), Mr. Ola Olukoyede, has said that the enactment of appropriate policy and regulation can tame cybercrime activities, including financial crimes, without applying the necessary enforcement strategies.

Olukoyede, who said this during the inauguration of the Awka Zone of the EFCC in Anambra State, insisted that past experience has shown that the application of the right policies and regulation have helped Nigeria in curbing cybercrimes and financial crimes without enforcement by the EFCC.

Citing the policy that established the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) for tertiary institution students, the EFCC boss said, that singular policy has drastically reduced cybercrime that was prevalent among young Nigerians who indulge in cybercrime activities, just to pay their school fees and survive on campus.

“Before NELFUND was established by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, most of the people that commit cybercrime ‘419’, are the youth. Majority of them are students of tertiary institutions and when we bring them forward for questioning as to why they indulge in cybercrimes, some of them genuinely tell us they can’t afford to pay their school fees, and that they needed money to pay their school fees and survive on campus because their parents are poor and cannot afford to pay their school fees,” Olukoyede said.

According to him, to curb the situation, President Tinubu directed that the proceeds of crime be channeled to support NELFUND. He said, that right policy has helped

hundreds of thousands of students to pay their school fees, adding that the implication is that the federal government has been able to take close to one million of the student beneficiaries out of the docket of the people that have the potential to commit cybercrimes.

“That is the effect of a single policy of the federal government that has pulled several students out of cybercrime activities, without involving the EFCC implementation strategies,” he said.

The EFCC boss also cited another instance with the fuel subsidy removal by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu.

“Upon the assumption of office, Mr. President made a policy statement and said:

‘Fuel subsidy is gone’. And I will tell you the implication of that on financial crimes investigation and prosecution in Nigeria. Before the fuel subsidy removal, we have about 80 cases of fuel subsidy in court. And some of those cases were filed way back 2013, 2014, and 2015, and we are still investigating the cases. We have been able to deal with less than 20 per cent of those cases in court as I speak and we don’t know whether we’re going to bring that to an end.

“But since the policy statement on the removal of fuel subsidy, the cases of financial crimes on fuel subsidy have dropped completely and that is the best way to fight corruption,” Olukoyede said.

According to him, some Nigerians still argue that EFCC must deal with the corruption rather than removing the fuel subsidy. He however said in fraud management, “there is what we call the principle of responsive elasticity, which says you should make a choice,” adding that he will rather stick with the right policy that eliminates corruption, than to continue fighting corruption that has been entrenched in the system for too long.

“So, these are some of the ways to fight corruption and financial crimes, and not just about law enforcement. Policy and regulations can block the leakages, going through standard procurement processes. These are the ways that we are also introducing into the regime because we are convinced that EFCC cannot defeat corruption alone,” Olukoyede further said.

He therefore called for ethical reorientation of the Nigerian people and advised political leaders, opinion leaders, civil societies, and traditional rulers to join the EFCC and the federal government in addressing cybercrime and financial crime activities in the country.

He said such collaboration would prevent fraudulent transactions before citizens lose their savings, strengthen procurement systems before public resources are diverted, and interrupt criminal financial flows before they mature. He added that the collaboration would also save the nation of enormous economic and social costs.

He reassured the people of Anambra State that the establishment of the EFCC Awka Zone, would not witch-hunt the good people of the state, but would rather enforce the law professionally and courageously, to protect the citizens of the state and its environs, such that their finances and that of government will be protected for the good of the people.

“The EFCC Awka Zone will engage government institutions, businesses, financial institutions, professional bodies, schools, markets, civil society organisations, traditional rulers, traditional institutions, religious bodies, and communities. It will educate stakeholders, build relationships, and mobilise the people to hold the fight against all forms of corrupt practices in the zone,” the EFCC boss said.

World.title: Jayden Adams’s girlfriend hints at conflict: ‘He isn’t here to protect’
World.content:
Jayden Adams and his partner, Aqueelah Adendorf with their daughter. Images via IG

Jayde Adams’s girlfriend, Aqueela Adendorf, has hinted at being mistreated by the late soccer star’s family following the shock death a few months ago.

The former Bafana Bafana player reportedly took his own life in July, shortly after the national team’s return from the FIFA World Cup, where they had played in the US and Mexico.

Jayden left behind two children – a five-year-old daughter with his partner, and a toddler son with another woman.



JAYDEN ADAMS’S GIRLFRIEND HINTS AT CONFLICT

On her TikTok account, Aqueelah Adendorf hinted at enduring family conflict, almost three months after Jayden Adams’s shock death.

The mother-of-one posted pictures of her daughter, Allaia-Jayda, implying that all was not well.

She shared: “She was the apple of her daddy’s eye, his little girl, his whole heart. 😩 He would never have allowed the things that are happening now, and it hurts knowing he isn’t here to protect her the way he always would have. 💔

She continued: “People say they care, but when it truly matters, you see who actually does. No one could ever replace her dad. But I’ll continue to protect her, love her and make sure she never feels alone. She has me, and I’ll always be there for her”.

Under the post, Aqueelah liked comments saying she had been “excluded” from family events and had to raise her daughter without the “resources” of her famous father. Another comment which she liked read: “Family turn into monsters”.

Jayden Adams’s partner also received the support of fellow Bafana Bafana and Sundowns WAG, Imaan Rayers, the wife of Iqraam Rayners, who commented: “You know that I’ll be here regardless. I love you”



TOMBSTONE REVEAL

Last month, the family of Jayden Adams unveiled his tombstone at his grave in the Jamestown Cemetery in Stellenbosch.

Jayden’s parents and loved ones wore Sundowns soccer T-shirts with his surname, “Adams,” printed on the back.

On his tombstone was a picture of Jayden donning his Sundowns kit as he lifted the CAF Champions League title.

In pictures posted on her social media accounts, Aqueelah is seen wearing white, whilst consoling her five-year-old daughter.

She shared: “It’s just you and me now, my girl. I never imagined I’d have to raise you without your daddy, but I promise I’ll give you all the love, strength and protection you need”.

She added: “You’ll never have to wonder if you’re loved. Mommy’s got you, always”.

Jayden’s other baby mama also shared pictures from the occasion.

World.title: Leaner gives Da Cruz a headache as Chiefs face Petersen decision
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs head coach Fernando Da Cruz could have a headache having to choose between Renaldo Leaner and Brandon Petersen in goals.

With Petersen injured last month, Leaner stepped in and has received widespread praise after making an assured debut in goal for Amakhosi in their 0-0 Betway Premiership draw against Lamontville Golden Arrows.

Before Petersen’s injury, the Amakhosi captain made a number of costly errors which led to goals. Some fans called for the captain to be benched but Da Cruz made it clear that the Cape Town-born keeper will remain his number one.



Leaner, who arrived at Naturena in July after leaving Sekhukhune United, was drafted in at relatively short notice due to the unfortunate injury suffered by Kaizer Chiefs captain.

“It was really exciting for me to play my first game because it has always been a dream for me to play for Kaizer Chiefs, one of the biggest teams in South Africa,” Leaner tolf www.kaizerchiefs.com.

Leaner took his opportunity with both hands, making two particularly good close-range saves that kept Amakhosi in the game and commanding his penalty area with authority throughout the 90 minutes.

Chiefs might have to drop Petersen for Learner

The former Sekhukhune United keeper explained how he remained calm in goals on his debut.

“I was able to make those saves because I went into the game with confidence and was very focused, which made me ready for action,” he says.

“I see a bright future for myself where I can become a better goalkeeper in the future and achieve great things in my career,” he says.



Amakhosi will be back in action next Tuesday against Stellenbosch at FNB stadium at 19:30. It remains to be seen if Leaner or Petersen will be in goals for Chiefs next week.

World.title: Jacob Zuma hospitalised in KZN: Here’s what we know
World.content:
Former president Jacob Zuma has been hospitalised in KwaZulu-Natal, with the MK Party moving to allay concerns over his health. Image: Flickr

Former president Jacob Zuma has been hospitalised in KwaZulu-Natal, with the MK Party moving to allay concerns over his health.

Zuma was admitted to hospital after campaigning in the province this week.

The MK Party says the 84-year-old underwent a routine medical check-up and is well.



However, reports surrounding his admission differ.

JACOB ZUMA HOSPITALISED

Initial reports indicated that Zuma had taken ill while campaigning in Msinga on Tuesday before being admitted to hospital.

A report states that an eyewitness saw Zuma arrive at hospital by ambulance.

However, the MK Party has played down concerns over the former president’s condition.

Party spokesperson Sifiso Mahlangu said Zuma undergoes routine medical checks twice a year.

“The president is not unwell. He is very much well and alive; it was a regular check-up,” Mahlangu said.



The party also said Zuma was in good spirits and expected to return to the campaign trail .

MK PARTY SAYS ZUMA IS WELL

Mahlangu said he had spoken to Zuma and maintained there was no cause for alarm.

He said Zuma had undergone routine checks, including blood tests.

According to another report, a family associate said that Zuma had been feeling unwell, but that his condition was not serious.

The associate said the hospital visit coincided with his scheduled medical check-up.

Other reports indicated that Zuma had already been discharged and returned to his Nkandla home.

The MK Party has not disclosed further details about the former president’s health.

ZUMA ON THE CAMPAIGN TRAIL

Zuma remains the leader and public face of the MK Party as South Africa heads towards the local government elections.

He has been campaigning in KwaZulu-Natal ahead of the polls.

The former president served as South Africa’s head of state from 2009 until his resignation in February 2018.

He later backed the newly formed MK Party ahead of the 2024 general elections and subsequently became its leader.

Zuma’s latest hospital visit comes as the party steps up its campaign ahead of the local government elections.

The MK Party maintains that Zuma is well and plans to resume campaigning on Friday.

World.title: SA confident about finances but cautions about debt
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - South Africans are feeling financial confidence, despite higher interest rates and record high petrol prices.

That's according to the 2026 Sanlam Financial Confidence Index.

But the report has found that consumers are taking less risks with credit.

READ | Consumers urged to settle debt amid paused rate hike

Home loan ownership has fallen from 21% to 14% year on year with personal loans, overdrafts and vehicle finance also down.

Behavioural scientist Kele Boakgomo said South Africans are defending what they have.

World.title: IMF says indebted governments must tighten their belts
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The International Monetary Fund has called on governments to reign in their borrowing.

It comes amid growing debt issues around the world due to higher interest rates.

IMF managing director Kristalina Georgieva was speaking before IMF and World Bank annual meetings to be held in Bangkok next week.

READ | Reserve Bank hikes interest rates by 25 basis points

She said that debt levels are the highest they've been since the second world war and governments need to make tough political choices.

Yields on government bonds in the US - effectively the interest rate on the debt - have jumped in recent weeks.

It sparked concern that governments will have to give investors bigger paybacks to loan money.

Fears around France's debt position has dropped the Euro to a 17-month low in recent days.

World.title: Inter-Ministerial Committee meets after ConCourt ruling on asylum seekers
World.content:
JOHANNEBSURG - The Inter-Ministerial Committee (IMC) is expected to convene what it calls an urgent meeting following the Constitutional Court ruling on the processing of asylum applications.

Deputy government spokesperson, William Baloyi said the meeting held this Wednesday evening includes legal experts and key stakeholders to carefully consider the implications of the judgment and to identify a lawful, practical and sustainable way forward.

In July, the apex court ruled that parts of the Refugee Act were unconstitutional and invalid.

It found that any person seeking asylum cannot be denied access to the system for failing to provide the required documents or to report to a refugee reception office within the stipulated five-day window.

READ | Constitutional Court finds parts of Refugee Act unconstitutional

Baloyi said they are fully aware of the matter and are treating it with urgency.

“IMC on Migration is acutely aware of the uncertainty, concern, panic and confusion that have arisen following the recent Constitutional Court judgment concerning asylum seekers and the impugned provisions of the Refugees Act... “South Africans should be assured that government remains committed to maintaining the integrity of our migration system, upholding the rule of law and safeguarding national interest,” he added.

Earlier in the day, a protest was held outside Home Affairs’ Refugee Reception Centre in Durban.

Protesters demanded an end to asylum applications being processed at the facility.

They wanted the centre to stop accepting and processing asylum claims for foreign nationals.

World.title: Sibiya's bail hearing stalls
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The state's case against suspended Deputy National Commission Shadrack Sibiya has tightened with a wave of digital evidence.

The 16-year-old complainant's father, Mr M, who worked as Sibiya's bodyguard, has revealed that he has almost 300 recordings of the disgraced top cop.

He said he had been keeping evidence records of Sibiya’s criminal activities

The court heard that Mr M also preserved photo evidence, vehicle-camera footage and vehicle-tracking information.

Sibiya’s wife, Sizakele Dlamini, filed an affidavit in the Randburg Magistrate’s Court claiming Mr M threatened her and said he would release documents about Sibiya to the police.

Mr M claimed that he had been documenting Sibiya’s movements and possessed sensitive information regarding certain individuals’ disappearances, of which Sibiya was allegedly aware of.

Meanwhile, prosecutors have shut down Sibiya's claim of consensual sex with an 18-year-old because the teenager wasn't sober at the time.

The state has welcomed the defence's evidence placed on record.

The material includes WhatsApp messages and audio recordings that the state says implicate the top cop.

The case has been postponed to Tuesday, a day after Sibiya's expected SAPS disciplinary hearing.

For now, he remains in custody.

eNCA reporter Pule Letshwiti-Jones has more details in the video above.

World.title: OUTA opposes plan to slash fuel levy for RAF
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - OUTA has warned that reducing the Road Accident Fund (RAF) levy will do little to fix the fund’s deepening financial crisis.

According to OUTA CEO Wayne Duvenage, RAF is underfunded but he argued that its problems are largely rooted in years of mismanagement, rising costs and maladministration spanning over a decade.

Duvenage comments come as the Department of Transport announced the consideration of a new funding model for the troubled fund, including a possible reduction in the RAF levy.

But Duvenage opposes the plan.

“When it comes to paying an annual fee to feed a levy such as this, as opposed to small incremental amounts as you fill up each time, it's much easier to collect it in the fuel price than trying to get people to pay a thousand or two thousand rand at the end of the year when they come to license their car, which is another thousand rand. “So, we must find a solution to this problem, but the solution lies not necessarily in the revenue collection, it lies in the way the Road Accident Fund has been badly managed,” he said.

According to the RAF website, the main income it receives is a levy based on fuel sales known as the RAF Fuel Levy.

“The RAF fuel levy income is a charge levied on fuel throughout the country and the quantum of the RAF fuel levy per litre is determined by the National Treasury on an annual basis, whereas total fuel sales are influenced by a number of macro-economic factors," RAF said

There are two main variables that determine the income of RAF, this includes petrol and diesel sold per annum and the rate of the levy.

RAF explains how the levy can be viewed as a compulsory contribution to social security benefits which is used only for the specific purposes as provided for in legislation

World.title: Number Of The Day | 2% Down: Why The JSE Sell-Off Matters For The Rand And Fuel Prices | 07 October 2026
World.content:
Why A Falling JSE Can Reach Much Further Than Your Investment Portfolio

A bad day on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange can look like a story for traders and pension-fund managers. But when falling shares arrive alongside a weaker rand and rising oil prices, the consequences can travel quickly beyond the market and into ordinary household budgets.

That is what makes the current combination of pressures worth watching. The JSE fell more than 2% on Wednesday, with resource and financial shares among the sectors under strain. At the same time, the rand weakened as the US dollar strengthened, while global oil prices climbed. Reuters reported Brent crude above $102 a barrel during Wednesday's global market sell-off.

Those movements are connected.

When investors believe US interest rates may remain higher or rise further, dollar-denominated assets can become more attractive. That can strengthen the dollar and

put pressure on currencies such as the rand. For South Africa, a weaker currency matters because the country buys oil on international markets in dollars.

That means South Africans can be squeezed from two directions at once: the global price of oil can rise while each dollar also becomes more expensive in rand terms.

The fuel-price problem does not stop at the pump

This matters particularly now because motorists have already absorbed a substantial October fuel-price increase. South Africa's regulated fuel-price system reflects, among other factors, movements in international petroleum prices and the rand-dollar exchange rate. Reuters reported that petrol prices were set to rise by as much as 12% from 7 October, while wholesale diesel prices would increase by 10%.

Another sustained period of expensive oil and rand weakness would therefore matter well beyond motorists filling their tanks. Fuel is embedded in the cost of moving food, goods and people around the economy. Businesses facing higher transport and operating costs must decide whether to absorb those increases or pass some of them on to customers.

That is how a market story can become an inflation story.

The South African Reserve Bank is already paying close attention to that risk. Its October 2026 Monetary Policy Review says global inflation rose during the first half of the year as energy disruptions lifted transport and production costs. It expects South African inflation to remain above 5% until the second quarter of 2027 and warns that persistent fuel, administered-price and food shocks could become embedded in inflation expectations.

Interest rates make the chain even more important

The Reserve Bank raised its policy rate by 25 basis points in September to 7.25%, taking cumulative increases between April and October to 50 basis points. It has identified upside risks to inflation and specifically pointed to the renewed fuel-price shock.

That does not mean another petrol-price increase automatically produces another interest-rate hike. Monetary policy depends on a much wider set of economic conditions. But it explains why movements in oil, the rand and inflation expectations matter to anyone with debt.

Higher-for-longer interest rates affect home loans, vehicle finance, business borrowing and disposable income. What begins as volatility in currencies and commodities can eventually influence how much money households have left after servicing debt.

This is also why a 2% fall on the JSE should not be read simply as a scoreboard showing whether investors had a good or bad day. Markets are constantly repricing expectations about inflation, interest rates, currencies, company earnings and future economic conditions.

For South Africans, the more useful question is therefore not simply whether the JSE recovers tomorrow.

It is whether the uncomfortable combination underneath the sell-off — a strong dollar, a weaker rand, costly oil and persistent inflation pressure — begins to unwind, or settles in for longer.
