NEW DELHI/CHANDIGARH: A set of WhatsApp chats purportedly mentioning alleged monetary transactions and details of postings of senior Punjab govt officials, including multiple DSPs, has been included in CBI's dossier on CM Bhagwant Mann's OSD Rajbir Singh Ghuman as the agency prepares to interrogate him and five others named in the "cash-for-transfers" FIR.The buzz in Chandigarh Wednesday was that Ghuman had been asked to appear before CBI at 2.30pm, leading a media contingent to assemble outside the agency's Sector 30 office.Amid speculation about whether Mann's OSD had defied the summons, a CMO official said no such notice was served on him. Ghuman is under the scanner for alleged corruption through intermediaries, including co-accused Nitin Gohal, Jitin, Romi Raja Mahajan, Bir Devinder and RS Nagra. According to an ED investigation prior to Punjab and Haryana high court calling in CBI, Gohal coordinated the bribery network.CBI's FIR mentions ED's "post-seizure questioning" of Gohal in May. He has been accused of receiving and forwarding drafts of orders and policies to "private individuals" prior to govt issuing an official release. One of these policies pertains to "foodgrain labour and cartage", which was allegedly shared by Gohal with co-accused Nagra, who has a foodgrain supply business.Nagra is accused of asking for favourable changes in the policy through Gohal, per the FIR.CBI has also obtained other purportedly incriminating documents about real estate projects, cooperative housing and irregularities in the Greater Mohali Area Development Authority, suggesting interference by "multiple private individuals" in govt functioning. CBI's probe focuses on allegations of corruption by influencing transfers, including those of IAS and IPS officers, matters pertaining to policy formulation, tender conditions, revenue and land-related issues in lieu of pecuniary benefits.

World.title: Medical trips costliest in both rural & urban areas
World.content:
Health and medical trips were most expensive among all trips completed in a year with average expenditure of Rs 29,454 in rural areas and Rs 41,649 in urban areas. Of this expenditure, over 70% was spent on medical treatment.

The largest chunk of travel (48.7%) in a year was for pilgrimage or religious purposes.

This was revealed in the survey on Domestic Tourism Expenditure conducted from July 2025 to June 2026 as part of National Sample Survey's 80th round. The survey collected information on purpose and expenditure of domestic travel, including overnight trips, and same-day journeys, and categories of expenditure during the trips.

The report showed that of the expenditure on travel for health and medical needs, 10% was for accommodation, followed by 5% each for food and drink and transport. For two other major categories of travel - holidaying, leisure and recreation, and for pilgrimage and recreation - transport was the largest chunk of expenditure. In case of overnight trips for shopping, the biggest chunk of expenditure was not surprisingly on shopping.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines





Rented or hired transport was the most popular for medical and health-centred trips accounting for almost 47% of trips in rural areas and about 40% in urban areas, followed by buses - 26% in rural areas and 21% in urban. Those surveyed used their own vehicle in less than a quarter of these trips in urban areas and less than one in five in rural.

Average expenditure per same-day trip, incurred by households in rural and urban areas, was highest for trips undertaken for 'shopping' (Rs 1,795 for rural, Rs 2,631 for urban) and 'health and medical' accounted for the second costliest purpose (Rs 1,499 for rural, Rs 1,859 for urban). For same-day trips, travel for health and medical needs figured after travel for social purpose and shopping.

World.title: Attacks on Saudi airports claimed by Houthi rebels kill 3 people, officials say
World.content:
Two attacks on airports in Saudi Arabia claimed by Iran-backed Houthi rebels in neighbouring Yemen killed three people Wednesday (October 7, 2026), Saudi officials said, as the kingdom was pulled deeper into the latest front in the Iran war.

The Saudi General Authority for Civil Aviation did not blame any party for the attacks at Abha and Riyadh’s King Khalid international airports, but Houthi rebels took credit earlier for the airport strikes.

The attack on Abha airport killed Moroccan and Algerian residents and wounded 28 other people, while the attack on King Khalid airport killed a Sudanese national and wounded eight other people, officials said.

As Riyadh has been targeted over the past week, new cage-like fences have been erected around fuel tanks and other equipment of the Saudi state-run Aramco oil company near the capital’s airport. The kingdom, the world’s top oil exporter, has seen oil and military assets targeted in recent days, posing a threat to crucial shipping alternative to the Strait of Hormuz, where traffic has been curtailed due to the Iran war.

The spokesperson for the Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis, Maj. Gen. Turki al-Malki, said forces intercepted a ballistic missile north of Riyadh and destroyed a platform in Yemen’s capital of Sana that had been used to launch attacks on the Saudi capital. The AP could not independently verify these claims.

Saudi Arabia and allied Yemeni forces launched a major ground and air offensive aimed at retaking territory that the rebels seized a month ago along Yemen’s western Red Sea coast and on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.

Those positions gave the Houthis better surveillance as they pursue a blockade of Saudi-linked shipping. On Monday, officials said forces of the Saudi-led coalition recaptured several key areas around the strait, through which about 12% of global trade transits.

World.title: Tanker off Qatar reports hits from multiple projectiles: U.K. maritime agency
World.content:
A tanker sailing off the north coast of Qatar reported being struck "by multiple projectiles", causing an unspecified number of casualties, the UKMTO maritime agency said on Wednesday (October 7, 2026).

The incident took place 51 nautical miles (94 kilometres) off the coast of the tiny Gulf state, the British agency said, adding that authorities were investigating. It did not specify the origin of the ship.

The reported attack on Wednesday (October 7, 2026) was around 500 kilometres (300 miles) from the Strait of Hormuz.

Ships in the Gulf and those attempting to transit the strait, the only way in or out of the oil-rich region for vessels, have come under repeated attack since the U.S. and Israel sparked the West Asia war in late February.

Iran has blockaded the strait ever since and fired on vessels it accuses of unauthorised crossings.

The United States has set up its own counterblockade of Iranian ports and occasionally fires on vessels linked to Tehran.

It has also bombed Iranian targets in retaliation for Tehran's attacks on ships, although there have been no such reported strikes since September 1.

Some vessels continue to ply the strait and U.S. media has reported on American efforts to protect ships on a route hugging the coast of Oman.

Diplomatic efforts to resolve the war, which began with a massive wave of surprise U.S.-Israeli strikes against Iran, have been deadlocked for months.

Hormuz is vital to the world economy, with around a fifth of the planet's oil and liquefied natural gas passing through the strait before the war began.

World.title: Jaishankar discusses bilateral ties with Cote d'Ivoire
World.content:
External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar on Wednesday (October 7, 2026) held talks with Cote d'Ivoire's Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation Niale Kaba on strengthening bilateral ties, with a focus on trade, infrastructure, agriculture and healthcare.

The Minister arrived in Cote d'Ivoire from Ghana on the second leg of his three-nation tour of African countries, which also includes Ethiopia.

Mr. Jaishankar said he had "comprehensive discussions" with Kaba in Abidjan on advancing India-Cote d'Ivoire partnership, "including in trade, investment, infrastructure, agriculture, healthcare and people-to-people ties".

"Underlined that our people-centric cooperation will be driven by the priorities of Cote d'Ivoire," he said in a social media post.

The two sides also discussed deepening their engagement in multilateral fora, he said.

Earlier, in Ghana, Jaishankar received from Foreign Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa the country's Instrument of Acceptance for the International Big Cat Alliance (IBCA).

IBCA is an India-led global initiative aimed at conserving seven major big cat species — tiger, lion, leopard, snow leopard, cheetah, jaguar and puma — and their habitats.

India launched the IBCA in 2023 to mark the 50th anniversary of Project Tiger.

The alliance seeks to bring together countries that are home to big cats as well as others interested in supporting their conservation, with cooperation envisaged in areas such as research, knowledge-sharing, capacity building and wildlife management.

Mr. Jaishankar also paid tribute at the Kwame Nkrumah Memorial in Accra, honouring Ghana's first Prime Minister and later president Kwame Nkrumah, a key figure in Africa's independence movement and one of the leading advocates of pan-Africanism.

Nkrumah, who led Ghana to independence from British colonial rule in 1957, played a prominent role in promoting solidarity among newly independent Asian and African countries.

He was also closely associated with the Non-Aligned Movement and the broader idea of South-South cooperation.

"The memorial and the museum showcase Dr Kwame Nkrumah’s vision of reliance, dignity and freedom. They also remind us of the importance of deeper South-South cooperation," Mr. Jaishankar said.

World.title: Nose of IndiGo plane found damaged after landing at Lucknow airport, lightning strike suspected
World.content:
An IndiGo aircraft operating flight 6E925 from Patna to Lucknow was found to have sustained damage to its nose section after landing at the Lucknow airport on Wednesday (October 7, 2026), with all 104 passengers on board safe, officials said.

"The aircraft landed normally around 4 pm and there were no reports of any injuries. The damage was noticed by the airport team after landing, following which the IndiGo team was informed and the aircraft was declared Aircraft on Ground (AOG)," an official told PTI, citing preliminary information.

"The aircraft is undergoing a technical inspection and further necessary action. As part of the preliminary assessment, the possibility of the aircraft encountering lightning during adverse weather conditions is being examined," the airport official added.

Further technical details will be shared by the airline after the completion of its investigation, according to a source.

The incident did not involve an emergency landing and the aircraft landed normally at the Lucknow airport, the source added.

World.title: Delhi HC asks Centre to consider plea for body-worn cameras for police managing protests, crowd
World.content:
The Delhi High Court on Wednesday (October 7, 2026) asked the Centre to consider a representation a petition seeking standard operating procedures for police and rapid action force personnel to use ‘always-on’ body-worn cameras during crowd-control and protest-management duties.

The court asked the government to communicate its decision to the petitioner within six months, while disposing of the public interest litigation (PIL).

The court was hearing the PIL, filed by advocate Chahat Raghav, seeking direction for constitution of an expert committee to formulate a binding SOP, making the use of body-worn cameras mandatory and continuous (always-on) for every member of Delhi Police and Rapid Action Force deployed on crowd-control, protest-management or dispersal duty, from the commencement of deployment until stand-down.

The plea also sought a comprehensive regime governing the storage, integrity, retention and evidentiary use of footage recorded through such cameras.

During the hearing, the court asked how the absence of body-worn cameras affects the rights of public at large.

To this, senior advocate Akhil Sibal, representing the petitioner, said when violence occurs there are allegations and counter allegations of violence and the issue pertains to accountability as to who is perpetrating violence and the use of excessive force by police.

He said there has to be some way for fixing the accountability.

Mr Sibal said cameras are being used by police officials but they are used in a very sporadic way. He said use of cameras was essential because allegations of excessive force used by police or protestors running and doing violence keep surfacing.

“We need a system so that the allegations are not left to private persons who are videographing,” Mr Sibal added.

Additional Solicitor General (ASG) Chetan Sharma submitted that there were guidelines for organising protests in which videography aspect was taken care of.

The petitioner said the plea has been filed in the backdrop of the July protests at Jantar Mantar involving the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and climate activist Sonam Wangchuk.

The plea said in the July protests, the use of force by Delhi Police and Rapid Action Force (RAF) upon student protesters was documented almost entirely through unofficial mobile-phone footage recorded by bystanders.

World.title: SC to hear Centre’s plea against Jharkhand DGP appointments
World.content:
Chief Justice of India Surya Kant agreed on Wednesday (October 7, 2026) to urgently hear a Union government plea that the State of Jharkhand is appointing Directors General of Police (DGPs) in defiance of a series of judicial orders passed by the Supreme Court since the past 20 years.

The Union government, through the Home Ministry, has also sought a judicial declaration that the ‘Selection and Appointment of Director General and Inspector General of Police, Jharkhand (Head of Police), Regulation of 2025’ be declared ultra vires the apex court’s Prakash Singh versus Union of India judgment of 2006. The 2006 judgment had laid down guidelines and directed a transparent appointment process for appointment of DGP from among senior most empanelled police officers of the State, and a minimum tenure of two years in a bid to rid the police of political influence.

The Centre pointed to the appointments of Anurag Gupta and Tadasha Mishra as the Jharkhand DGPs on the basis of “this ultra vires Regulations,” allegedly in violation of the Prakash Singh judgment.

“Both the Regulation framed by the State of Jharkhand and the appointments made thereunder are legally infirm, as they are not in conformity with the existing rules and contrary to the specific directions issued by the Supreme Court,” the application said.

The application has sought a direction to the State of Jharkhand to company with the Prakash Singh judgment, and further declare the appointments of DGPs pursuant to the 2025 Regulation as illegal.

World.title: Cornell students stage sit-in to protest university’s handling of alleged 2024 gang rape
World.content:
Some Cornell students staged a sit-in at a dining hall and vowed not to spend money on campus on Wednesday (October 7, 2026) to protest sexual violence and how the university has handled complaints, in the latest expression of outrage over an alleged 2024 gang rape at a fraternity house.

A handwritten sign reading “Justice for Jane Doe ” — the name under which the accuser is suing — was propped on an empty table in the dining hall in the afternoon. Some students sat around the room without eating, while others lunched. Another small group sat outside holding signs with messages such as “we are Jane Doe.”

Groups organising the demonstration intended to keep the sit-in going for seven hours.

The demonstrations were meant to spotlight complaints that the university is slow to respond to reports of sexual assault while quick to protect its reputation. Among other demands, the groups want the university to retool disciplinary procedures for addressing complaints and expel or revoke the degrees of anyone involved in the alleged October 2024 sexual assault.

Jane Doe, who was a student then, alleges that Chi Phi members plied her with alcohol and drugs and several sexually assaulted her. One man sent others a message inviting them to participate, according to a lawsuit she filed last month against Cornell, the fraternity, seven men who were Chi Phi brothers and others.

Lawyers for two of the men have denied they participated in a sexual assault. Attempts by The Associated Press to reach the others or their representatives have been unsuccessful. Some of the men who underwent a university disciplinary hearing in 2024 told investigators that the sexual activity was consensual or said they were not involved.

The woman went to Cornell police in November 2024, though no criminal charges resulted. In the wake of her lawsuit, the state attorney general is conducting a renewed criminal investigation.

Cornell closed down the Chi Phi campus chapter in 2024 and says it expelled some students and suspended others after an investigation under the federal Title IX law.

This week Cornell trustees brought in former U.S. Deputy Attorney General Sally Yates to review how the school investigates sexual assault and sexual harassment, how the disciplinary process works, campus police response and more.

World.title: Brazilian students in Rio de Janeiro march against the prospect of another Bolsonaro presidency
World.content:
Thousands of Brazilian students marched in downtown Rio de Janeiro on Wednesday (October 7, 2026) to protest against the possibility of Flávio Bolsonaro winning the presidency, after the far-right candidate received more votes than incumbent and left-leaning Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in the first round of Brazil’s presidential election.

A sea of red-clad demonstrators made their way between two historical squares in Rio’s center, chanting and holding signs referencing Brazil’s sovereignty and democracy in the South American country, which they said were under threat.

“We’re fighting for Brazil, not for Lula,” said Talita Amaral, a 19-year-old environmental science student at a nearby university. She was wearing Brazil’s yellow and green soccer jersey, often worn by supporters of Bolsonaro, which she said was a gesture aimed at reclaiming the national colors.

“We don’t have time to be sad, we need to be doing this, occupying the streets, sending messages in WhatsApp groups, trying to convince people,” Amaral said, as the chant “Olé olé olé ola, Lula Lula” rang out across Cinelandia square.

Neither Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro who is serving a 27-year sentence for attempting a coup, nor Lula received more than the required 50% of the vote needed to become Brazil’s leader on Sunday. Therefore, they will face each other in an unpredictable runoff on Oct. 25.

But Flávio Bolsonaro has at least two advantages: He received 2 million more votes than Lula on Sunday and the candidates who placed third, fourth and fifth are all on the right of the political spectrum. They gathered 6 million votes between them.

Mr. Bolsonaro is under investigation for corruption, money laundering and tax evasion because of his ties to the failed Banco Master — a case that many protesters in Rio made reference to on Wednesday.

Some pointed to Jair Bolsonaro's handling of the coronavirus pandemic, during which 700,000 people were reported to have died from the disease, while others held signs emblazoned with messages such as “Brazil isn't anyone's backyard” and “I don't vote for someone who sells Brazil.”

Many on the left fear a Flávio Bolsonaro presidency would fully align the Brazilian government with the United States because of the proximity in ideologies between U.S. President Donald Trump and the Bolsonaro family. Last year, Trump imposed a 50% tariff on Brazilian goods and imposed sanctions on a Brazilian Supreme Court justice, citing Jair Bolsonaro’s trial, which he called a “witch hunt.”

“If Bolsonaro wins, Brazil will become a colony of the United States,” said João Victor Vieira, 20, who studies literature. He said that Bolsonaro represented a threat to minorities such as people of color, women and the LGBTQ+ community. Bolsonaro's father was notorious for homophobic remarks.

Mr. Vieira said that while he was initially dispirited following the results on Sunday, he has since regained hope.

“This protest shows that social movements are still very much alive,” he said. “We will resist.”

World.title: DG ISPR says Pakistani troops present in Saudi Arabia 'for decades' across multiple domains
World.content:
Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) Director General Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry has said that Pakistani troops are in Saudi Arabia, adding that they had been in the kingdom “for decades” and across multiple domains.

The military spokesperson made these remarks during an interview with CNN correspondent Ivan Watson, who posted a small clip on his X account.

“I can confirm that the forces of Pakistan are already there (Saudi Arabia),” Lt Gen Chaudhry said.

Watson then sought a confirmation that Pakistani troops were already on the ground in Saudi Arabia as part of the Makkah Defence Alliance between Pakistan, the kingdom and Turkiye.

To that, the military spokesperson replied, “Pakistan troops have been there for decades […] The Makkah alliance is not something that has come out in a vacuum. So there is a sustained diplomatic, political, military and people-to-people relationship between Pakistan, Turkiye and Saudi Arabia. So, I can share with you that Pakistani forces, in multiple capabilities and domains, are already there.”

Lt Gen Chaudhry’s remarks come after Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye agreed to the deployment of military forces and capabilities rapidly in the kingdom during an emergency meeting of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement in Riyadh on Monday.

The three countries had held an emergency meeting of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee (SPDC) of the Makkah Defence Alliance to address the security developments and threats facing Saudi Arabia.

“The committee decided to move immediately to the practical implementation of the collective defence commitments and to take the necessary measures to provide the agreed military forces and capabilities and ensure their rapid deployment in the kingdom, in accordance with the approved arrangements and the national legislation of the parties, thereby enhancing readiness, military integration, and the collective capacity to confront and counter threats,” a statement issued by the Foreign Office after the meeting said.

While the statement did not specifically name any threat, the development comes against the backdrop of Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia in the Yemen conflict.

Separately, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif, who was part of Pakistan’s delegation in the meeting, joined Geo News programme ‘Aaj Shahzeb Khanzada Kay Saath’ via telephone the same day and said Saudi Arabia had made “gains and recovered some areas” in Yemen in the ongoing fighting with the Houthis.

When asked about a possible operational role by Pakistan and Turkiye, the defence minister replied that both nations had a “presence in theatre”, but only Saudi troops were involved in combat operations.

“Whatever assistance they require is being provided. But right now, the Turkish and Pakistani armies are playing a supportive role,” he said, noting that Pakistan was involved in reconnaissance.

Asif had earlier also reaffirmed that Pakistan would “practically and diplomatically” stand by Saudi Arabia against Yemen’s Houthi rebels if the situation escalated. The defence minister had said that Pakistan would fulfil all its obligations under the Makkah Defence Alliance in accordance with the terms of the agreement between the three countries.

The Makkah defence pact , signed on Aug 7, aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empower its signatory states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them.

On Sept 25, the military chiefs of alliance members Pakistan, Turkiye and Saudi Arabia met in Riyadh for urgently convened talks under the pact in light of the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.

World.title: Govt raises petrol price by Rs1.82 per litre, reduces high-speed diesel rate by Re0.91
World.content:
The government on Wednesday raised the price of petrol by Rs1.82 per litre, but reduced that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Re0.91 per litre.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs396.65 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs394.94 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices are applicable for Oct 8 (Thursday).

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm and fuel allocations for official vehicles has been cut by 50 per cent for three months.

On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices.

Previously, on July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: 3 killed in attacks on Saudi Arabia's King Khalid, Abha airports: civil aviation body
World.content:
Saudi authorities said on Wednesday that three people were killed in attacks on two of the kingdom’s international airports including in the capital Riyadh, after Yemen’s Houthis claimed to have fired on both transport hubs.

The Houthis earlier took responsibility for a flurry of attacks that included firing a ballistic missile at Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport as the conflict deepens with Saudi Arabia, which backs Yemen’s government.

“On Tuesday and Wednesday… Abha International Airport and King Khalid International Airport were subjected to attacks targeting their facilities,” the kingdom’s civil aviation authority said in a statement, without blaming anyone for the attacks.

An Egyptian and an Algerian national were killed at Abha airport and a Sudanese national was killed at the airport in Riyadh, the agency said, with 36 people wounded in the attacks.

Those injured in the attack on King Khalid International Airport included five Saudi citizens, two Egyptians and a Pakistani, the statement said.

The Saudi-led coalition that backs pro-government forces in Yemen said on X that it “destroyed the ballistic missile launch platform” used in the attack on Riyadh.

The Houthis, who control most of the country’s northwest, are battling for territory against the Saudi-backed forces after the civil war reignited in July and they captured swathes of coastal land.

The fighting has displaced more than 200,000 people within the country, the United Nations said on Wednesday.

Yemen’s internationally recognised government this week declared a major counter-offensive and said Houthi fighters were pushed out of strategic areas on the Red Sea and the port city of Mocha.

But the Houthis say they are holding their territory, and military sources from both sides contacted by AFP have not reported any major changes on the ground.

Claims by the warring parties have been impossible to independently verify with the situation moving fast and access for journalists difficult.

“Our armed forces have just targeted King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh with a ballistic missile. The strike was accurate, by God’s grace, and led to a disruption of air traffic,” Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said Wednesday in a post on X.

The Saudi-led military coalition that backs Yemen’s government had said the missile was intercepted.

In a separate post the Houthis also said they targeted a military supply convoy near the airport in the Yemeni city of Aden, the interim capital for the government.

The Yemeni government’s Saba news agency reported missiles and drones targeting that airport.

The agency cited transport authorities as saying one of the missiles landed near the runway minutes before the scheduled arrival of a flight from Cairo, which was forced to divert to Jeddah in Saudi Arabia.

Houthi drones and missiles also targeted Saudi Arabia’s Abha airport and King Khalid Air Base in Khamis Mushait, spokesman Saree said, claiming they had “hit their targets accurately”.

It is the second time this week that the Houthis claimed to have attacked the main airport in the Saudi capital.

It is facing frequent temporary closures of its airspace, according to tracking website Flightradar24.

Saudi Arabia leads an international coalition that has been fighting the Houthis since 2015, and is now trying to roll back the group’s latest advance.

On Monday, the coalition said it was providing air support for the counter-offensive launched by the Yemeni government forces.

After a four-year ceasefire, Yemen’s civil war re-erupted in July. Last month the Houthis seized the entire western coastline along the Red Sea in the country’s deadliest fighting in years.

On Wednesday, new clashes in Yemen’s west left at least 62 combatants dead, including 37 Houthis, military sources from both camps told AFP.

The government’s Saba news agency also said the Houthis fired a missile at the city of Taiz, which is held by government forces, wounding five civilians.

“We went out into the street to check on the wounded and saw young civilians who had been hit. The Houthi shell landed in the middle of the street, right in an area crowded with civilians,” Taiz resident Al-Fateh al-Eisaei told AFP.

Yemen’s government has announced a goal of retaking all Houthi territory, home to most of the country’s population, and much of it held for more than a decade.

The humanitarian crisis caused by the war has left most of the nation’s population dependent on aid.

Mohammed, a 33-year-old charity worker who fled from Mocha to Aden, told AFP on Tuesday that “people there are terrified” of the Houthis.

“Life in Mocha has come to a complete standstill,” he said.

World.title: Emergency, governor's rule would 'definitely' be imposed if deemed necessary to 'save' KP: Kundi
World.content:
Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi said on Wednesday that if the prime minister and the president deemed it necessary to impose an emergency or governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa to “save the province” facing terrorism, it would “definitely be enforced”.

The governor’s remarks came during Geo News’ programme ‘Aaj Shahzeb Khanzada Kay Saath’, where the possibility of emergency or governor’s rule was discussed.

Responding to questions on the subject, Kundi argued that there had been past instances of emergency and governor’s rule being imposed.

“In Balochistan, the PPP had to end its government for law and order and impose an emergency,” he remarked.

Asked whether an emergency or governor’s rule would be sustainable if imposed, Kundi replied: “The first thing [to decide] is when and whether it is imposed. We can discuss its sustainability in another programme.”

This prompted the host to prod Kundi further, saying his remarks indicated that only imposing an emergency or governor’s rule was being considered and its sustainability would addressed later.

Kundi said in response, “We have to save the province, we have to establish peace in the province.”

The Centre has warned the PTI-led KP government in recent days of sending it packing through an emergency or governor’s rule as the party goes ahead with a protest march to demand the release of its jailed founder, Imran Khan. Federal ministers have also cited the security situation in KP in this connection, as reiterated by Kundi.

Meanwhile, the march remains a major bone of contention between the government and the main opposition party in the Centre, the PTI, with both taking entrenched positions.

On Sunday, Interior Mini­ster Mohsin Naqvi also called on Kundi to discuss the political and security situation amid speculations of ‘imminent’ governor’s rule in the province.

The meeting was also mentioned in the Geo News programme, with Kundi being asked whether preparations were under way for an emergency or governor’s rule. But Kundi said the PTI’s long march and security-related matters were discussed during the meeting.

The KP governor then went on the accuse the provincial government of “facilitating terrorism” and not doing enough to curb it.

World.title: CDF Munir reaffirms Pakistan’s commitment to international peace in meeting with UN chief
World.content:
Chief of Army Staff and Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir on Wednesday reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to international peace in a meeting with United Nations Secretary General Antonio Guterres, the military’s media affairs wing said.

The UN secretary general is currently in Islamabad on a two-day official visit.

In a statement on Wednesday, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said Guterres called on CDF Munir at the General Headquarters (GHQ) in Rawalpindi.

“During the meeting, matters of mutual interest, the prevailing regional security environment and the UN’s role in promoting international peace and security were discussed,” it said.

“The two sides exchanged views on regional stability, the Jammu and Kashmir dispute, India’s abeyance of the Indus Waters Treaty and terrorism emanating from Afghanistan,” it added.

During the meeting, CDF Munir also reaffirmed “Pakistan’s commitment to international peace and highlighted its contributions to UN peacekeeping missions”. He also lauded the UN’s role in “advancing peace, stability and humanitarian cooperation”.

According to ISPR, the UN secretary general paid tribute to the sacrifices and contributions of Pakistan and its armed forces in the war against terror and in UN peacekeeping missions.

“He also acknowledged Pakistan’s continued commitment to international peace and security,” ISPR said, adding that Guterres specifically appreciated “Pakistan’s efforts towards the peaceful resolution of regional conflicts”.

UN chief meets PM Shehbaz

Later, the UN secretary general also met Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, who lauded Guterres for his “principled commitment to the UN Charter, multilateralism, international law, dialogue and the peaceful settlement of disputes”, a statement by the PM’s Office said.

It added that the premier acknowledged the UN chief’s “outstanding contribution to international peace and security during his tenure”.

PM Shehbaz also reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to an “effective, inclusive and representative UN, particularly at a time when multilateralism faces significant challenges”, the statement added.

Welcoming Guterres’ UN80 Initiative, he emphasised that UN reforms should be responsive to the priorities of developing countries, while strengthening conflict prevention, peaceful settlement of disputes, peacekeeping and peacebuilding.

Additionally, the premier also reaffirmed Pakistan’s longstanding contribution to UN peacekeeping and the maintenance of international peace and security.

“The prime minister highlighted Pakistan’s diplomatic efforts to promote dialogue and de-escalation, including its mediation role between the US and Iran,” the statement read, adding that PM Shehbaz reiterated that dialogue and diplomacy remain the only viable path to resolving disputes.

PM Shehbaz also reiterated the need for a peaceful resolution of the Jammu and Kashmir dispute, in accordance with relevant UN Security Council resolutions and the wishes of the Kashmiri people.

“He highlighted that the Indus Waters Treaty is a binding international agreement and that India’s unilateral decision to place it in abeyance has no legal basis,” the statement added.

Moreover, PM Shehbaz, noting that a peaceful and stable Afghanistan remains in Pakistan’s interest, expressed serious concern over the presence of terrorist groups and terrorism emanating from Afghan territory and emphasised the need for concrete and verifiable actions against such elements.

Reaffirming Pakistan’s steadfast support for Palestinian self-determination and statehood, PM Shehbaz reiterated Islamabad’s support for the implementation of the Gaza Peace Plan and UNSC Resolution 2803, which endorses the end of Israel’s military campaign in the Gaza Strip.

“The prime minister also underscored the need for greater access to affordable and concessional financing for developing countries to advance development and climate resilience,” the PMO stated.

According to the statement, Secretary General Guterres appreciated Pakistan’s longstanding contribution to the organisation and international peace and security, including its role in UN peacekeeping and the Security Council.

“He particularly appreciated Pakistan’s diplomatic efforts to promote dialogue, mediation and de-escalation, and welcomed its continued commitment to multilateralism and the purposes and principles of the UN Charter,” the statement read.

On the first day of his trip, the UN secretary general held a meeting with Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar. During the meeting, Guterres appreciated Pakistan’s “longstanding contribution to the UN, as well as its diplomatic efforts to promote dialogue, mediation and de-escalation”.

He also addressed a joint stakeout with Dar, during which he lauded Pakistan’s “pivotal role” in mediating between the United States and Iran as he called on the parties to end the conflict and return to diplomacy.

President Asif Ali Zardari also conferred the Nishan-i-Imtiaz on Guterres in recognition of his “distinguished international service, leadership of the UN and contribution to global peace and development”.

The two also held a separate meeting, where Zardari appreciated Guterres’ principled leadership, his efforts for international peace, dialogue, diplomacy and peaceful settlement of disputes, as well as his constructive engagement with Pakistan and attention to the concerns of developing countries.

World.title: Will not allow military operations, KP CM tells march participants in Khyber
World.content:
The PTI convoy led by Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Sohail Afridi reached the Khyber district on Wednesday with the provincial chief executive vowing that he would not allow another military operation in KP.

The route plan for the march, being carried out to demand the release of jailed PTI founder Imran Khan, has been changing since it began.

The PTI earlier planned that the chief minister would lead his convoy to Khairabad — which borders Punjab’s Attock — on Oct 8 and announce the next plan of action.

However, according to a statement released by CM Afridi’s office, he told the protesters in Khyber today that the long march would now go all the way to Swabi, where he would announce the next plan of action.

But a member of the PTI’s social media team, Omar Farooq, told Dawn that the final destination remained tentative for now.

He also confirmed that the march will reach Peshawar on Thursday and spend the night tomorrow in Charsadda. The plan was also shared by the focal person to the chief minister on social media, Yar Muhammad Khan Niazi.

PTI MNA Sajid Khan Mohmand told Dawn that the CM would reach Mohmand on Oct 9 and address a gathering at Mian Mandi Bazaar on Oct 10.

The march was announced as part of the PTI’s nationwide protest, initially scheduled for Sept 27 but was later postponed to Oct 4.

On Oct 4, the march began from Lakki Marwat and Karak, from where the protesters trekked to Kohat on the second day and arrived in Mattani, located on the outskirts of Peshawar, on Tuesday night.

While the plan for the trek after Oct 8 is yet to be announced, the PTI previously announced Islamabad as its final destination.

The Centre has warned the party against any protest or gatherings in Islamabad. However, the PTI decided to embark on the march after weekend talks with the federal government to bridge their differences failed for multiple reasons , particularly over the counterterrorism policy.

KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi again challenged the PTI today to go through Swabi, saying, “Let them cross through Swabi and show us”, while speaking on Geo News programme ‘Aaj Shahzeb Khanzada Kay Saath’.

Afridi decries military operations

“I will not allow another military operation in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa; I will resist anti-people policies till I am the chief minister,” Afridi said while addressing PTI supporters in Khyber.

Khyber is also home to Tirah, whose residents had agreed to vacate their homes to facilitate a military operation against terrorists in December 2025.

In recent months, the displaced families have expressed reservations over the government’s fulfilment of commitments following their displacement, including the provision of financial assistance.

The KP government, led by the PTI, has also been opposed to military operations in the province. Now, it also finds itself at odds with the Centre over the latter’s counterterrorism policy — a sticking point that is said to have led to the breakdown of negotiations between the federal government and the opposition in the Centre, including the PTI.

Mentioning those talks, the KP chief minister alleged in his address that attempts were made to compel the provincial government to 

“The people of Tirah were displaced in extreme winter,” he said, and added without naming anyone that “they did not have any realisation of the hardships faced by the people”.

CM Afridi claimed that people were happy in tribal areas before military operations, recalling that PTI founder and ex-prime minister Imran Khan had been voicing opposition to those operations since 2004.

He also decried what he described as the provision of insufficient funds for erstwhile tribal areas by the Centre, claiming that his government had released Rs21 billion for families affected by military operations.

Noting that the KP government was being accused of not cooperating on counter-terrorism, he argued that terrorism was also prevalent in Balochistan, where the provincial government was cooperating with the Centre.

He reiterated his allegation that the Centre had not released the funds allocated for the erstwhile tribal areas, including Khyber, after their merger with KP.

Additional input from Mohammad Ashfaq and Fauzee Khan

World.title: Bahrain's foreign minister arrives in Islamabad for 2-day visit
World.content:
Bahraini Foreign Minister Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani arrived in Islamabad on Wednesday evening for a two-day visit, where he is expected to co-chair the third session of the Joint Ministerial Commission (JMC), the Foreign Office (FO) said.

According to the FO, Al Zayani was received at the airport by Economic Affairs Division Secretary Muhammad Humair Karim and Additional Secretary (Middle East) Zahid Hussain.

“The visit reflects the close, cordial and brotherly ties between Pakistan and Bahrain and underscores the shared commitment to further strengthening bilateral cooperation,” it added.

In an earlier statement, the FO said that Bahrain’s top diplomat will be visiting the country at the invitation of Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar.

“The two sides will review the entire spectrum of bilateral relations and discuss ways to further strengthen cooperation across diverse areas of mutual interest, including trade, investment, economic cooperation, defence and security, labour and manpower, and cultural exchanges,” it said.

The two sides would also exchange views on regional and international developments of mutual interest and cooperation at multilateral forums, the FO added.

“Pakistan and Bahrain enjoy close, brotherly relations founded on shared faith, common values, mutual respect, and longstanding people-to-people links,” it noted.

The FO further stated that the two countries maintain regular high-level exchanges and close cooperation across a wide range of areas.

“The visit reflects the strong momentum in Pakistan-Bahrain relations and the shared commitment of both countries to further deepen bilateral cooperation and advance mutually beneficial ties,” it said.

Earlier this month, Dar chaired an inter-ministerial meeting to review preparations for the Pakistan-Bahrain JMC, which he will co-chair with his Bahraini counterpart.

The deputy premier had directed the ministries concerned to finalise preparations in close coordination and pursue concrete outcomes from the Bahrain FM’s visit.

Dar and Al Zayani last met in September on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York, where they discussed bilateral relations, including preparations for the forthcoming JMC session.

They also exchanged views on regional and international developments, with Al Zayani appreciating Pakistan’s constructive role in promoting regional peace and stability.

Following the last JMC session in July 2021, which was held in Manama, the two countries signed a memorandum of understanding to promote business between the two countries.

Islamabad and Manama had agreed to establish the JMC in 2014, when King Sheikh Hamad bin Isa bin Salman Al-Khalifa paid a three-day visit to Pakistan.

World.title: Remaining 3 Pakistanis rescued from hijacked vessel off Somalia return home
World.content:
The three remaining Pakistani crew members of MT Honour 25, an oil tanker that was hijacked off the coast of Somalia in April, landed in Karachi on Wednesday.

According to Shaheen Burney, the vice chairperson of the Ansar Burney Trust, the three crew members arrived in the city at 4:40pm via an Ethiopian Airways flight from Addis Ababa.

Sindh Governor Nehal Hashmi welcomed the crew members at Karachi’s Jinnah International Airport upon their return, according to a press release. Karachi Mayor Murtaza Wahab and other dignitaries were also present.

The governor met the returning Pakistanis, inquired about their well-being and presented them with bouquets. He expressed solidarity with them, saying that the incident was extremely painful and highlighting that the “sufferings and hardships of the affected Pakistanis were being shared as a collective national concern”, the statement said.

Speaking to the media, the governor said that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had taken special notice of the matter, issued necessary directives and remained continuously informed about the situation of the affected Pakistanis.

He said that, although no amount of money could compensate for the loss of a human life, the state would take “all possible measures” to support the affected families, particularly with regards to the education, healthcare and future of their children.

PM Shehbaz had issued clear directions regarding residential plots and arrangements for the education, upbringing and healthcare of the children of the affected families, he added, according to the press release.

Hashmi noted that the state would extend support to the affected families as far as possible, while any financial assistance received in this regard would also be given to the affected persons. The provincial government had also extended its full cooperation, he said.

“We are not here as representatives of any political party; we are here as Pakistanis. We have come to express solidarity with our brothers and assure them that they are not alone — the entire nation stands with them,” the statement quoted the governor as saying.

He added that the incident had once again demonstrated that “a united nation could face any kind of difficult situation”. He also prayed for the complete and speedy recovery of the returning Pakistanis.

In late September, the maritime police force of Somalia’s semi-autonomous Puntland recovered the Palau-flagged oil tanker, which had 19 crew members on board, including 10 Pakistanis.

Of those 10, the Foreign Office (FO) confirmed that three were among five crew members who died during the operation. Another four Pakistanis who were injured returned to the country on Sunday along with the remains of their three colleagues, with the government facilitating their repatriation via Ethiopia.

In an earlier post on X, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said the remaining three crew members of MT Honour 25 — Imran Ali, Husain Yousuf and Muhammad Yasin — were “en route to safely return home to Karachi from Addis Ababa later today and will be reunited with their families”.

He said the Pakistani ambassador in the Ethiopian capital “met the three crew members and ensured that they were provided all necessary facilities and services during their stay” in Addis Ababa.

Dar noted that the FO and the government, under the leadership of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, “made every effort to secure the safe return of all our crew members”.

“While we welcome the safe return of our people, we remain deeply saddened by the loss of three Pakistani crew members. May Allah grant them eternal peace and give strength to their families.”

FM Dar reaffirmed that Pakistan “remains firmly committed to working with international partners to combat piracy and ensure the safety and security of seafarers and maritime routes”.

Apart from Pakistanis, the vessel’s crew also included seven Indonesians, an Indian and a Sri Lankan. After the April hijacking, months passed with no progress either in negotiations or the payment of the ransom, said to be around $3 million, for the recovery of the hostages.

The hostages were said to be victims of an “ ownership crisis ”, as it was not clearly established who owned the ship — the man previously thought to be an owner was later revealed to be more likely a middleman who hired them.

During its ordeal, the crew made several emotional videos and audio appeals , reporting that they had run out of clean water, food and medicine. Meanwhile, their families launched an international appeal, calling on foreign governments, the United Nations (UN) and the International Maritime Organisation (IMO) to take coordinated action to help secure the release of their loved ones.

For its part, FO maintained that it had remained “actively engaged” to secure the release of the sailors.
